title: Śrīmad Bhāgavatam — Canto 3: The Status Quo

topics.name: Chapter 1: Questions by Vidura

questions.question: After renouncing his prosperous home and entering the forest, to whom did King Vidura address his questions?
questions.explanation: "After renouncing his prosperous home and entering the forest, King Vidura, the great devotee, asked this question of His Grace Maitreya Rsi." (SB 3.1.1)

questions.question: Why did King Dhrtarastra set fire to the lacquer house to burn the fatherless Pandavas?

options.text: Under the influence of impious desires to nourish his dishonest sons

questions.explanation: "King Dhrtarastra became blind under the influence of impious desires to nourish his dishonest sons, and thus he set fire to the lacquer house to burn his fatherless nephews, the Pandavas." (SB 3.1.6)

questions.question: Whose hair did Duhsasana grab, an abominable act the King did not forbid?
questions.explanation: "The King did not forbid his son Duhsasana's abominable action of grabbing the hair of Draupadi, the wife of the godly King Yudhisthira." (SB 3.1.7)

questions.question: After Yudhisthira was unfairly defeated in gambling, why did he go off to the forest?

options.text: Because he was banished by Krsna
Because he had taken the vow of truthfulness

questions.explanation: "But because he had taken the vow of truthfulness, he went off to the forest." (SB 3.1.8)

questions.question: Whom did Vidura describe as breathing heavily like a snake while waiting with Yudhisthira?
questions.explanation: "He is waiting with his younger brothers, among whom is the revengeful Bhima, breathing heavily like a snake." (SB 3.1.11)

questions.question: Of whom did Vidura tell Dhrtarastra that he was maintaining offense personified as his infallible son?
questions.explanation: "You are maintaining offense personified, Duryodhana, as your infallible son, but he is envious of Lord Krsna." (SB 3.1.13)

questions.question: When Vidura gave his wise instructions, who insulted him, swollen with anger and with trembling lips?
questions.explanation: "Vidura, whose personal character was esteemed by respectable persons, was insulted by Duryodhana, who was swollen with anger and whose lips were trembling." (SB 3.1.14)

questions.question: After being insulted, what did Vidura do upon leaving his brother's palace?

options.text: He drew his sword and fought
He placed his bow on the door and quit the palace

questions.explanation: "Vidura placed his bow on the door and quit his brother's palace." (SB 3.1.16)

questions.question: After leaving Hastinapura, what did Vidura take shelter of?
questions.explanation: "After leaving Hastinapura, he took shelter of many places of pilgrimages, which are the Lord's lotus feet." (SB 3.1.17)

questions.question: At which place of pilgrimage did Vidura learn that all his relatives had died?
questions.explanation: "At the place of pilgrimage at Prabhasa, it came to his knowledge that all his relatives had died due to violent passion." (SB 3.1.21)

questions.question: After learning of his relatives' deaths, in which direction did Vidura proceed, toward which river?

options.text: West, where the river Sarasvati flows

questions.explanation: "After this he proceeded west, where the river Sarasvati flows." (SB 3.1.21)

questions.question: How many places of pilgrimage on the bank of the river Sarasvati did Vidura visit?
questions.explanation: "On the bank of the river Sarasvati there were eleven places of pilgrimage." (SB 3.1.22)

questions.question: On the bank of which river did Vidura meet Uddhava, the great devotee of Lord Krsna?
questions.explanation: "At last he reached the bank of the Yamuna, where he happened to meet Uddhava, the great devotee of Lord Krsna." (SB 3.1.24)

questions.question: Of whom was Uddhava formerly a great student?
questions.explanation: "Vidura embraced him [Uddhava], who was a constant companion of Lord Krsna and formerly a great student of Brhaspati's." (SB 3.1.25)

questions.question: Pradyumna, the commander in chief of the Yadus, was who in a former life?
questions.explanation: "How is Pradyumna, the commander in chief of the Yadus, who was Cupid in a former life?" (SB 3.1.28)

questions.question: In a previous birth, Samba was born as whom, in the womb of the wife of Lord Siva?
questions.explanation: "In a previous birth he was born as Karttikeya in the womb of the wife of Lord Siva, and now he has been born in the womb of Jambavati." (SB 3.1.30)

questions.question: From whom did Yuyudhana learn the intricacies of the military art?
questions.explanation: "He learned the intricacies of the military art from Arjuna and attained the transcendental destination which is very difficult to reach even for great renouncers." (SB 3.1.31)

questions.question: Which devotee fell down on the dust of a road marked with the footprints of Lord Krsna, due to his ecstasy of transcendental love?
questions.explanation: "He once lost his mental equilibrium due to his ecstasy of transcendental love and fell down on the dust of a road which was marked with the footprints of Lord Krsna." (SB 3.1.32)

questions.question: About whom did Vidura lament as one who 'rebelled against his brother after death' and drove Vidura out of his own house?
questions.explanation: "I simply lament for him [Dhrtarastra] who rebelled against his brother after death." (SB 3.1.41)

questions.question: In whose family did the unborn Lord appear by His causeless mercy, only for their interest?
questions.explanation: "Only for their interest did He appear in the family of His unalloyed devotees the Yadus." (SB 3.1.45)

topics.name: Chapter 2: Remembrance of Lord Krsna

questions.question: When Vidura asked Uddhava to speak on the messages of Lord Krsna, why was Uddhava unable to answer immediately?

options.text: Due to excessive anxiety at the remembrance of the Lord
Because he did not know the answer
Because he was angry with Vidura
Because he was tired from traveling

questions.explanation: "Uddhava was unable to answer immediately due to excessive anxiety at the remembrance of the Lord." (SB 3.2.1)

questions.question: At what age was Uddhava so absorbed in the service of Lord Krsna that he did not wish to take his morning breakfast when called by his mother?
questions.explanation: "He was one who even in his childhood, at the age of five years, was so absorbed in the service of Lord Krsna that when he was called by his mother for morning breakfast, he did not wish to have it." (SB 3.2.2)

questions.question: What did Vidura observe Uddhava trying to wipe away from his eyes, signifying total ecstasy?

options.text: Tears of separation from the Lord
Tears of joy at meeting Vidura

questions.explanation: "Uddhava had all the transcendental bodily changes due to total ecstasy, and he was trying to wipe away tears of separation from his eyes." (SB 3.2.5)

questions.question: How did Uddhava describe Lord Krsna's disappearance, calling Him the sun of the world?

options.text: He has gone to the forest
The sun of the world, Lord Krsna, has set

questions.explanation: "My dear Vidura, the sun of the world, Lord Krsna, has set, and our house has now been swallowed by the great snake of time." (SB 3.2.7)

questions.question: To what did Uddhava compare the Yadu dynasty's failure to identify Lord Hari as the Personality of Godhead?

options.text: A blind man missing the path
A fish that could not identify the moon
A bird that cannot see the sky
A child who cannot recognize fire

questions.explanation: "They could not identify Lord Hari as the Personality of Godhead, any more than the fish could identify the moon." (SB 3.2.8)

questions.question: By which internal potency did the Lord appear in the mortal world in His eternal form?
questions.explanation: "The Lord appeared in the mortal world by His internal potency, yoga-maya." (SB 3.2.12)

questions.question: When Krsna left the damsels of Vraja, what happened to them?

options.text: They sat down with stunned intelligence and could not finish their household duties

questions.explanation: "They used to follow Him with their eyes, and thus they sat down with stunned intelligence and could not finish their household duties." (SB 3.2.14)

questions.question: When Krsna went away from His father's protection to Vraja, why did He live there incognito?

options.text: Out of fear of the enemy

questions.explanation: "How He went away from His father's protection to Vraja and lived there incognito out of fear of the enemy." (SB 3.2.16)

questions.question: From whom did Lord Krsna beg pardon for His inability to serve their feet, due to being away from home out of fear of Kamsa?
questions.explanation: "Lord Krsna begged pardon from His parents for Their inability to serve their feet, due to being away from home because of great fear of Kamsa." (SB 3.2.17)

questions.question: Who, the King of Cedi, achieved success in yoga practice although he hated Lord Krsna?
questions.explanation: "You have personally seen how the King of Cedi [Sisupala] achieved success in yoga practice, although he hated Lord Krsna." (SB 3.2.19)

questions.question: How did the fighters on the Battlefield of Kuruksetra who saw Krsna's lotuslike face achieve the abode of the Lord?

options.text: Purified by the onslaught of Arjuna's arrows

questions.explanation: "Others who were fighters on the Battlefield of Kuruksetra were purified by the onslaught of Arjuna's arrows." (SB 3.2.20)

questions.question: What pained Uddhava to remember about how Krsna behaved before King Ugrasena?

options.text: That He used to stand and submit explanations before him while Ugrasena sat on the throne
That He was rebuked by Ugrasena

questions.explanation: "He used to stand before King Ugrasena, who was sitting on the royal throne, and used to submit explanations before him." (SB 3.2.22)

questions.question: To whom did Lord Krsna grant the position of mother although she prepared deadly poison to be sucked from her breast?
questions.explanation: "He who granted the position of mother to a she-demon [Putana] although she was unfaithful and she prepared deadly poison to be sucked from her breast." (SB 3.2.23)

questions.question: In whose womb was Lord Krsna begotten by Vasudeva, in the prison of the King of Bhoja?
questions.explanation: "Lord Sri Krsna... was begotten by Vasudeva in the womb of his wife Devaki in the prison of the King of Bhoja." (SB 3.2.25)

questions.question: For how many years did Krsna live in the cow pastures of Maharaja Nanda like a covered flame with His elder brother Baladeva?
questions.explanation: "There He lived for eleven years like a covered flame with His elder brother, Baladeva." (SB 3.2.26)

questions.question: Who engaged the great wizards able to assume any form to kill Krsna?
questions.explanation: "The great wizards who were able to assume any form were engaged by the King of Bhoja, Kamsa, to kill Krsna." (SB 3.2.30)

questions.question: Which chief of the reptiles poisoned a certain portion of the Yamuna, distressing the inhabitants of Vrndavana?
questions.explanation: "A certain portion of the Yamuna was poisoned by the chief of the reptiles [Kaliya]." (SB 3.2.31)

questions.question: Whom did Krsna want to give a lesson by advising His father to perform worship of the cows and pasturing land?
questions.explanation: "Also He wanted to give a lesson to Indra, the King of heaven." (SB 3.2.32)

questions.question: With what did the compassionate Lord Krsna save the inhabitants of Vraja when Indra poured water incessantly?

options.text: His pastime umbrella, the Govardhana Hill

questions.explanation: "The compassionate Lord Krsna saved them from danger with His pastime umbrella, the Govardhana Hill." (SB 3.2.33)

questions.question: In which season did the Lord enjoy as the central beauty of the assembly of women, attracting them with His pleasing songs?

options.text: The third season of the year, an autumn night brightened by moonshine

questions.explanation: "In the third season of the year, the Lord enjoyed as the central beauty of the assembly of women by attracting them with His pleasing songs in an autumn night brightened by moonshine." (SB 3.2.34)

topics.name: Chapter 3: The Lord's Pastimes Out of Vrndavana

questions.question: After going to Mathura with Baladeva, how did Krsna kill Kamsa to please Their parents?

options.text: By shooting him with an arrow
By dragging him down from his throne and pulling him along the ground
By cutting off his head with the chakra
By drowning him in the Yamuna

questions.explanation: "They dragged Kamsa, the leader of public enemies, down from his throne and killed him, pulling him along the ground with great strength." (SB 3.3.1)

questions.question: From whom did the Lord learn all the Vedas simply by hearing them once?
questions.explanation: "The Lord learned all the Vedas with their different branches simply by hearing them once from His teacher, Sandipani Muni." (SB 3.3.2)

questions.question: Rukmini, whom Krsna carried away, was the daughter of which king?
questions.explanation: "Attracted by the beauty and fortune of Rukmini, the daughter of King Bhismaka, many great princes and kings assembled to marry her." (SB 3.3.3)

questions.question: By subduing seven bulls whose noses were not pierced, whose hand did the Lord achieve?
questions.explanation: "By subduing seven bulls whose noses were not pierced, the Lord achieved the hand of Princess Nagnijiti in the open competition to select her bridegroom." (SB 3.3.4)

questions.question: Just to please His dear wife, what did the Lord bring back from heaven, just as an ordinary husband would do?
questions.explanation: "Just to please His dear wife, the Lord brought back the parijata tree from heaven, just as an ordinary husband would do." (SB 3.3.5)

questions.question: Narakasura, killed by the Lord, was the son of whom?
questions.explanation: "Narakasura, the son of Dharitri, the earth, tried to grasp the whole sky, and for this he was killed by the Lord in a fight." (SB 3.3.6)

questions.question: What did the princesses kidnapped by Narakasura offer when they saw the Lord, the friend of the distressed?
questions.explanation: "They looked upon Him with eagerness, joy and shyness and offered to be His wives." (SB 3.3.7)

questions.question: How many offspring did the Lord beget in each and every one of His wives?
questions.explanation: "The Lord begot in each and every one of them ten offspring with exactly His own qualities." (SB 3.3.9)

questions.question: When Kalayavana, the King of Magadha and Salva attacked Mathura, why did the Lord refrain from killing them personally?

options.text: Just to show the power of His own men

questions.explanation: "The Lord refrained from killing them personally, just to show the power of His own men." (SB 3.3.10)

questions.question: Of the demons Sambara, Dvivida, Bana, Mura, Balvala and Dantavakra, how did the Lord deal with them?

options.text: He caused all to be killed by others
Some He killed Himself, and some He caused to be killed by others
He banished them from the kingdom

questions.explanation: "Some He killed Himself, and some He caused to be killed by others [Sri Baladeva, etc.]." (SB 3.3.11)

questions.question: What was the great burden of the earth, eighteen aksauhinis, abated with the help of Drona, Bhisma, Arjuna and Bhima?
questions.explanation: "The abatement of the earth's great burden, eighteen aksauhinis, has now been effected with the help of Drona, Bhisma, Arjuna and Bhima." (SB 3.3.14)

questions.question: According to the Lord, how would the great strength of the Yadu dynasty finally disappear?

options.text: By a great war with the demigods
When they quarrel among themselves, influenced by intoxication

questions.explanation: "When they quarrel among themselves, influenced by intoxication, with their eyes red like copper because of drinking [madhu], then only will they disappear." (SB 3.3.15)

questions.question: Whom did Lord Krsna establish in the position of supreme control of the world to show the ideal of administration on the path of piety?
questions.explanation: "Lord Sri Krsna... established Maharaja Yudhisthira in the position of supreme control of the world in order to show the ideal of administration on the path of piety." (SB 3.3.16)

questions.question: The embryo begotten by Abhimanyu in the womb of Uttara was burnt by whose weapon, but later protected by the Lord?
questions.explanation: "The embryo of Puru's descendant begotten by the great hero Abhimanyu in the womb of Uttara, his wife, was burnt by the weapon of the son of Drona, but later he was again protected by the Lord." (SB 3.3.17)

questions.question: How many horse sacrifices did the Supreme Lord induce the son of Dharma (Yudhisthira) to perform?
questions.explanation: "The Supreme Lord induced the son of Dharma to perform three horse sacrifices." (SB 3.3.18)

questions.question: In conformity with which system of philosophy was the Lord situated in detachment and knowledge while enjoying life in Dvaraka?
questions.explanation: "He was situated in detachment and knowledge, as enunciated by the Sankhya system of philosophy." (SB 3.3.19)

questions.question: After many years of household life in Dvaraka, what was at last fully manifested in the Lord?

options.text: His detachment from ephemeral sex life
His wish to rule the world

questions.explanation: "The Lord was thus engaged in household life for many, many years, but at last His detachment from ephemeral sex life was fully manifested." (SB 3.3.22)

questions.question: Who can put faith in Lord Krsna's transcendental sense activities?

options.text: One who has become a devotee of the Lord by rendering devotional service

questions.explanation: "No one, therefore, can put his faith in Lord Krsna's transcendental sense activities but one who has become a devotee of the Lord by rendering devotional service." (SB 3.3.23)

questions.question: Why did the great sages curse the princely descendants of the Yadu and Bhoja dynasties?

options.text: Because they were made angry by the sporting activities of the princes, as desired by the Lord
Because the princes refused them charity

questions.explanation: "Great sages were made angry by the sporting activities of the princely descendants of the Yadu and Bhoja dynasties, and thus, as desired by the Lord, the sages cursed them." (SB 3.3.24)

questions.question: When the descendants of Vrsni, Bhoja and Andhaka went to Prabhasa, who remained in Dvaraka?

options.text: Those who were eternal devotees of the Lord

questions.explanation: "Those who were eternal devotees of the Lord did not leave but remained in Dvaraka." (SB 3.3.25)

topics.name: Chapter 4: Vidura Approaches Maitreya

questions.question: After partaking of the remnants of prasada, what liquor did the descendants of Vrsni and Bhoja drink, making them delirious?
questions.explanation: "All of them... partook of the remnants of prasada and also drank liquor made of rice." (SB 3.4.1)

questions.question: At what time of day did the interaction of the faults of intoxication cause their minds to become unbalanced and destruction to take place?
questions.explanation: "At sunset, by the interaction of the faults of intoxication, all their minds became unbalanced, and destruction took place." (SB 3.4.2)

questions.question: After foreseeing the end of His family, where did Lord Krsna go to sip water and sit down underneath a tree?

options.text: The bank of the river Sarasvati

questions.explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna, after foreseeing the end [of His family] by His internal potency, went to the bank of the river Sarasvati, sipped water, and sat down underneath a tree." (SB 3.4.3)

questions.question: Where had the Lord previously told Uddhava to go?
questions.explanation: "Thus He who desired to destroy His family told me previously to go to Badarikasrama." (SB 3.4.4)

questions.question: Why did Uddhava follow Krsna even though he knew of the Lord's desire to destroy the dynasty?

options.text: Because it was impossible for him to bear separation from the lotus feet of the master
Because he wanted to witness the destruction
Because he was afraid to be alone

questions.explanation: "I followed Him because it was impossible for me to bear separation from the lotus feet of the master." (SB 3.4.5)

questions.question: By which features did Uddhava immediately recognize the Lord as the Supreme Personality of Godhead?

options.text: His four hands, different symbolic representations, and yellow silk garments

questions.explanation: "I could immediately recognize Him as the Supreme Personality of Godhead by His four hands, different symbolic representations, and yellow silk garments." (SB 3.4.7)

questions.question: Against what kind of tree was the Lord sitting and taking rest in His final pastime?
questions.explanation: "The Lord was sitting, taking rest against a young banyan tree, with His right lotus foot on His left thigh." (SB 3.4.8)

questions.question: What did the Lord tell Uddhava (Vasu) about the association Uddhava had desired in days of yore?

options.text: That it was impossible to obtain
That it is very difficult for others to obtain, but He awards it unto him
That Uddhava must earn it through penance
That only Brahma could grant it

questions.explanation: "You particularly desired to achieve My association. This is very difficult for others to obtain, but I award it unto you." (SB 3.4.11)

questions.question: To which transcendental abode did the Lord tell Uddhava he could now go by leaving this universe?
questions.explanation: "Now you can go to My transcendental abode, Vaikuntha, by leaving this universe of conditioned living entities." (SB 3.4.12)

questions.question: To whom did the Lord say He had spoken His transcendental glories, described by sages as Srimad-Bhagavatam, at the beginning of creation?

options.text: Brahma, situated on the lotus from His navel

questions.explanation: "I spoke unto Brahma, who is situated on the lotus that grows out of My navel, about My transcendental glories, which the great sages describe as Srimad-Bhagavatam." (SB 3.4.13)

questions.question: Among the four principles of religiosity, economic development, sense gratification and liberation, what did Uddhava prefer to engage in only?

options.text: The loving service of the Lord's lotus feet

questions.explanation: "I have preferred only to engage in the loving service of Your lotus feet." (SB 3.4.15)

questions.question: What knowledge did Uddhava request the Lord to explain, which the Lord had explained before to Brahmaji?

options.text: Transcendental knowledge which gives enlightenment about the Lord

questions.explanation: "Kindly explain to us... that transcendental knowledge which gives enlightenment about Yourself and which You explained before to Brahmaji." (SB 3.4.18)

questions.question: Where did Uddhava say he was proceeding for association, as instructed by the Lord?
questions.explanation: "I am now proceeding to Badarikasrama in the Himalayas for association, as I have been instructed by Him." (SB 3.4.21)

questions.question: In which incarnation has the Personality of Godhead been undergoing great penance at Badarikasrama since time immemorial?

options.text: As the sages Nara and Narayana

questions.explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, in His incarnation as the sages Nara and Narayana, has been undergoing great penance since time immemorial for the welfare of all amiable living entities." (SB 3.4.22)

questions.question: From whom did Uddhava advise Vidura to take lessons for the reception of transcendental knowledge?
questions.explanation: "You may take lessons from the great learned sage Maitreya, who is nearby and who is worshipable for reception of transcendental knowledge." (SB 3.4.26)

questions.question: On the bank of which river did Uddhava pass the night with Vidura as if it were a moment, before going away?
questions.explanation: "After thus discussing with Vidura the transcendental name, fame, qualities, etc., on the bank of the Yamuna, Uddhava was overwhelmed with great affliction." (SB 3.4.27)

questions.question: According to Sukadeva Gosvami, the cursing of the brahmanas was only a plea, but what was the actual fact?

options.text: The supreme desire of the Lord

questions.explanation: "The cursing of the brahmanas was only a plea, but the actual fact was the supreme desire of the Lord." (SB 3.4.29)

questions.question: Why could Uddhava remain in this world to disseminate knowledge of the Personality of Godhead?

options.text: Because he was the eldest devotee
Because he is never affected by the modes of material nature
Because he was a great scholar

questions.explanation: "Uddhava is not inferior to Me in any way because he is never affected by the modes of material nature." (SB 3.4.31)

questions.question: Upon understanding that he was remembered by Lord Krsna while quitting this world, what did Vidura do?

options.text: He began to cry loudly, overwhelmed by the ecstasy of love

questions.explanation: "Understanding that he was remembered by Lord Krsna... Vidura began to cry loudly, overwhelmed by the ecstasy of love." (SB 3.4.35)

questions.question: After passing a few days on the bank of the Yamuna, on the bank of which river did Vidura reach where the great sage Maitreya was situated?
questions.explanation: "After passing a few days on the bank of the river Yamuna, Vidura, the self-realized soul, reached the bank of the Ganges, where the great sage Maitreya was situated." (SB 3.4.36)

topics.name: Chapter 5: Vidura's Talks with Maitreya

questions.question: At the source of which celestial river (Hardwar) did Vidura reach Maitreya, the fathomless learned sage?
questions.explanation: "Vidura... thus reached the source of the celestial Ganges river [Hardwar], where Maitreya, the great, fathomless learned sage of the world, was seated." (SB 3.5.1)

questions.question: What did Vidura observe that people gain from engaging in fruitive activities to attain happiness?

options.text: Neither satiation nor mitigation of distress; on the contrary they are only aggravated

questions.explanation: "Everyone in this world engages in fruitive activities to attain happiness, but one finds neither satiation nor the mitigation of distress." (SB 3.5.2)

questions.question: What did Vidura request Maitreya to narrate about how the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord of the three worlds, acts?

options.text: How He accepts incarnations and creates the cosmic manifestation with perfectly arranged regulative principles

questions.explanation: "Kindly narrate how the Supreme Personality of Godhead... accepts incarnations and creates the cosmic manifestation with perfectly arranged regulative principles for its maintenance." (SB 3.5.5)

questions.question: Although Vidura had heard about the higher and lower statuses of human society from Vyasadeva, with what was he NOT satisfied?

options.text: The nectar of topics about Krsna

questions.explanation: "They have not satisfied me with the nectar of topics about Krsna." (SB 3.5.10)

questions.question: According to Vidura, topics of the Lord can cut off one's bondage to family affection simply by what means?

options.text: By entering the holes of one's ears

questions.explanation: "Such topics can cut off one's bondage to family affection simply by entering the holes of one's ears." (SB 3.5.11)

questions.question: In which great work had Vyasa already described the transcendental qualities of the Lord?
questions.explanation: "Your friend the great sage Krsna-dvaipayana Vyasa has already described the transcendental qualities of the Lord in his great work the Mahabharata." (SB 3.5.12)

questions.question: Vidura lamented that people's duration of life is spoiled by eternal time while they involve themselves in what?

options.text: Philosophical speculation, theoretical ultimate goals of life, and different modes of ritual

questions.explanation: "I see how their duration of life is spoiled by eternal time while they involve themselves in presentations of philosophical speculation, theoretical ultimate goals of life, and different modes of ritual." (SB 3.5.14)

questions.question: To what did Vidura compare Maitreya's describing the essence of all topics, the topics of the Lord?

options.text: A river flowing to the sea
The sun rising in the morning
A bird returning to its nest

questions.explanation: "Just as bees collect honey from flowers, kindly describe the essence of all topics — the topics of the Lord." (SB 3.5.15)

questions.question: Maitreya said it was not wonderful that Vidura accepted the Lord without deviation of thought, because Vidura was born from the semen of whom?
questions.explanation: "It is not at all wonderful that you have so accepted the Lord without deviation of thought, for you were born from the semen of Vyasadeva." (SB 3.5.19)

questions.question: Due to the cursing of which muni was Vidura born, when formerly he was King Yamaraja?
questions.explanation: "I know that you are now Vidura due to the cursing of Manduvya Muni and that formerly you were King Yamaraja, the great controller of living entities after their death." (SB 3.5.20)

questions.question: Prior to the creation, how did the Personality of Godhead exist?
questions.explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, the master of all living entities, existed prior to the creation as one without a second." (SB 3.5.23)

questions.question: By what name is the external energy, through whose agency the entire material manifestation is made possible, known?
questions.explanation: "This external energy is known as maya or illusion, and through her agency only is the entire material manifestation made possible." (SB 3.5.25)

questions.question: When the transcendental purusa incarnation impregnates the material nature of three modes, what appears by the influence of eternal time?
questions.explanation: "The Supreme Living Being in His feature as the transcendental purusa incarnation... impregnates the material nature of three modes, and thus by the influence of eternal time the living entities appear." (SB 3.5.26)

questions.question: What is the great causal truth, the mahat-tattva, transformed into, which is manifested in three phases of cause, effect and the doer?
questions.explanation: "Mahat-tattva, or the great causal truth, transforms into false ego, which is manifested in three phases — cause, effect and the doer." (SB 3.5.29)

questions.question: The false ego is transformed into mind by interaction with which mode?
questions.explanation: "The false ego is transformed into mind by interaction with the mode of goodness." (SB 3.5.30)

questions.question: The sky is a product of what, which is the transformation of egoistic ignorance?
questions.explanation: "The sky is a product of sound, and sound is the transformation of egoistic ignorance." (SB 3.5.32)

questions.question: Earth, the final physical element, is qualified primarily by which quality?
questions.explanation: "Thus it was transformed into the earth, which is qualified primarily by smell." (SB 3.5.36)

questions.question: Why are the controlling deities of the physical elements, though empowered expansions of Lord Visnu, described as offering fascinating prayers to the Lord?

options.text: Because they were entrusted with different functions of universal duties and were unable to perform them

questions.explanation: "Because they were entrusted with different functions of universal duties and were unable to perform them, they offered fascinating prayers to the Lord as follows." (SB 3.5.38)

questions.question: In their prayer, to what did the demigods compare the Lord's lotus feet that protect the surrendered souls?
questions.explanation: "Your lotus feet are like an umbrella for the surrendered souls, protecting them from all the miseries of material existence." (SB 3.5.39)

questions.question: In the final verse, what did the demigods, created from the mahat-tattva, request of the Supreme Self?

options.text: Perfect knowledge and potency to render Him service in subsequent creation

questions.explanation: "Kindly award us Your perfect knowledge and potency so that we can render You service in the different departments of subsequent creation." (SB 3.5.51)

topics.name: Chapter 6: Creation of the Universal Form

questions.question: Why had the progressive creative functions of the universe been suspended, as the Lord heard?

options.text: Due to the curse of a sage
Due to the noncombination of His potencies, such as the mahat-tattva
Due to a great devastating flood
Due to the absence of Brahma

questions.explanation: "The Lord thus heard about the suspension of the progressive creative functions of the universe due to the noncombination of His potencies, such as the mahat-tattva." (SB 3.6.1)

questions.question: Into how many elements did the Supreme Lord simultaneously enter, along with the goddess Kali, His external energy?
questions.explanation: "The Supreme Powerful Lord then simultaneously entered into the twenty-three elements with the goddess Kali, His external energy, who alone amalgamates all the different elements." (SB 3.6.2)

questions.question: When the twenty-three principal elements were set in action by the will of the Supreme, what came into existence?

options.text: The gigantic universal form, or the visva-rupa body of the Lord

questions.explanation: "When the twenty-three principal elements were set in action by the will of the Supreme, the gigantic universal form, or the visvarupa body of the Lord, came into existence." (SB 3.6.4)

questions.question: The gigantic virat-purusa, known as Hiranmaya, lived for how long on the water of the universe?

options.text: A thousand cycles of four yugas

questions.explanation: "The gigantic virat-purusa, known as Hiranmaya, lived for one thousand celestial years on the water of the universe, and all the living entities lay with Him." (SB 3.6.6)

questions.question: The gigantic universal form of the Supreme Lord is described as the first incarnation and plenary portion of whom?
questions.explanation: "The gigantic universal form of the Supreme Lord is the first incarnation and plenary portion of the Supersoul." (SB 3.6.8)

questions.question: From which part of the gigantic form did Agni, or heat, separate?
questions.explanation: "Agni, or heat, separated from His mouth, and all the directors of material affairs entered into it in their respective positions." (SB 3.6.12)

questions.question: Which deity entered the two nostrils of the gigantic form, enabling living entities to smell?
questions.explanation: "When the Lord's two nostrils separately manifested themselves, the dual Asvini-kumaras entered them in their proper positions..." (SB 3.6.14)

questions.question: When the eyes of the gigantic form manifested, who entered them with the partial representation of eyesight?

options.text: The sun, the director of light

questions.explanation: "The sun, the director of light, entered them with the partial representation of eyesight, and thus the living entities can have vision of forms." (SB 3.6.15)

questions.question: When the genitals of the gigantic form manifested, who entered into them with his partial semen?
questions.explanation: "...then Prajapati, the original living creature, entered into them with his partial semen, and thus the living entities can enjoy sex pleasure." (SB 3.6.19)

questions.question: Which deity entered the hands of the gigantic form, enabling the living entity to transact business for his livelihood?

options.text: Indra, the ruler of the heavenly planets

questions.explanation: "...Indra, the ruler of the heavenly planets, entered into them, and thus the living entity is able to transact business for his livelihood." (SB 3.6.21)

questions.question: When the intelligence of the gigantic form manifested, who entered into it with the partial power of understanding?

options.text: Brahma, the lord of the Vedas

questions.explanation: "...Brahma, the lord of the Vedas, entered into it with the partial power of understanding, and thus an object of understanding is experienced by the living entities." (SB 3.6.23)

questions.question: Who entered the materialistic ego of the gigantic form as the controller of false ego?
questions.explanation: "...into it entered Rudra, the controller of false ego, with his own partial activities, by which the living entity transacts his objective actions." (SB 3.6.25)

questions.question: From which part of the gigantic form were the heavenly planets manifested?
questions.explanation: "...from the head of the gigantic form, the heavenly planets were manifested, and from His legs the earthly planets and from His abdomen the sky separately manifested themselves." (SB 3.6.27)

questions.question: The demigods, who reside in the heavenly planets, are qualified by which mode?

options.text: The superexcellent quality of the mode of goodness
A mixture of all three modes

questions.explanation: "The demigods, qualified by the superexcellent quality of the mode of goodness, are situated in the heavenly planets..." (SB 3.6.28)

questions.question: From which part of the virat form did the brahmanas, the natural teachers of society, come into existence?
questions.explanation: "...the Vedic wisdom became manifested from the mouth of the virat, the gigantic form. Those who are inclined to this Vedic knowledge are called brahmanas..." (SB 3.6.30)

questions.question: From which part of the gigantic virat form was the power of protection generated, in relation to which the ksatriyas came into existence?
questions.explanation: "...the power of protection was generated from the arms of the gigantic virat form, and in relation to such power the ksatriyas also came into existence..." (SB 3.6.31)

questions.question: The means of livelihood of the vaisyas, the production of grains and their distribution, was generated from which part of the Lord's form?
questions.explanation: "The means of livelihood of all persons, namely production of grains and their distribution to the prajas, was generated from the thighs of the Lord's gigantic form." (SB 3.6.32)

questions.question: The sudras, who satisfy the Lord by service, are situated on which part of the Personality of Godhead?
questions.explanation: "Situated on the legs are the sudras, who satisfy the Lord by service." (SB 3.6.33)

questions.question: After mature meditation for one thousand celestial years, what could Brahma, the original poet, know about the Supreme Soul?

options.text: That the glories of the Supreme Soul are inconceivable

questions.explanation: "...the original poet, Brahma, after mature meditation for one thousand celestial years, could know only that the glories of the Supreme Soul are inconceivable." (SB 3.6.38)

questions.question: According to the last verse, what failed to achieve success in knowing the Supreme Personality of Godhead?

options.text: Words, mind and ego, with their respective controlling demigods
The demigods in the heavenly planets

questions.explanation: "Words, mind and ego, with their respective controlling demigods, have failed to achieve success in knowing the Supreme Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.6.40)

topics.name: Chapter 7: Further Inquiries by Vidura

questions.question: Who expressed a pleasing request by asking a question while Maitreya was speaking?

options.text: Vidura, the learned son of Dvaipayana Vyasa

questions.explanation: "...Vidura, the learned son of Dvaipayana Vyasa, expressed a request in a pleasing manner by asking this question." (SB 3.7.1)

questions.question: Why is there no possibility of desire prompting the Lord to play, as boys are prompted to play?

options.text: Because He is busy with creation
Because He is self-satisfied and detached from everything at all times
Because He does not exist materially

questions.explanation: "But there is no possibility of such desire for the Lord because He is self-satisfied and detached from everything at all times." (SB 3.7.3)

questions.question: By what has the Lord caused the creation, maintenance and dissolution of this universe again and again?

options.text: By His self-sheltered potency of the three modes of material nature

questions.explanation: "By His self-sheltered potency of the three modes of material nature, the Lord has caused the creation of this universe." (SB 3.7.4)

questions.question: Vidura asked: the pure soul is pure consciousness and is never out of consciousness due to circumstances, time, situations or dreams. How then does he become engaged in what?
questions.explanation: "The pure soul is pure consciousness and is never out of consciousness, either due to circumstances, time, situations, dreams or other causes. How then does he become engaged in nescience?" (SB 3.7.5)

questions.question: Vidura asked: with the Lord as Supersoul situated in every living being's heart, why do the living entities' activities result in what?
questions.explanation: "The Lord, as the Supersoul, is situated in every living being's heart. Why then do the living entities' activities result in misfortune and misery?" (SB 3.7.6)

questions.question: How did Maitreya appear when he was first agitated by the inquisitive Vidura, before replying without hesitation?
questions.explanation: "...Maitreya, being thus agitated by the inquisitive Vidura, at first seemed astonished, but then he replied to him without hesitation, since he was fully God conscious." (SB 3.7.8)

questions.question: Maitreya said the living entity is in distress regarding his self-identity, having no factual background, like a man who dreams what?

options.text: That he sees his head cut off

questions.explanation: "The living entity is in distress regarding his self-identity. He has no factual background, like a man who dreams that he sees his head cut off." (SB 3.7.10)

questions.question: Maitreya compared the self associated with matter to which reflected object that appears to tremble due to the water?
questions.explanation: "As the moon reflected on water appears to the seer to tremble due to being associated with the quality of the water, so the self associated with matter appears to be qualified as matter." (SB 3.7.11)

questions.question: By whose mercy, through the process of devotional service in the mode of detachment, can the misconception of self-identity be gradually diminished?
questions.explanation: "But that misconception of self-identity can be diminished gradually by the mercy of the Personality of Godhead, Vasudeva, through the process of devotional service to the Lord in the mode of detachment." (SB 3.7.12)

questions.question: Simply by chanting and hearing of the transcendental name and form of which Personality of Godhead can one achieve the cessation of unlimited miserable conditions?
questions.explanation: "Simply by chanting and hearing of the transcendental name, form, etc., of the Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna, one can achieve the cessation of unlimited miserable conditions." (SB 3.7.14)

questions.question: According to Maitreya, who both enjoy happiness, while persons between them suffer the material pangs?

options.text: The lowest of fools and he who is transcendental to all intelligence

questions.explanation: "Both the lowest of fools and he who is transcendental to all intelligence enjoy happiness, whereas persons between them suffer the material pangs." (SB 3.7.17)

questions.question: By serving what is one enabled to develop transcendental ecstasy in the service of the Personality of Godhead?

options.text: The feet of the spiritual master

questions.explanation: "By serving the feet of the spiritual master, one is enabled to develop transcendental ecstasy in the service of the Personality of Godhead..." (SB 3.7.19)

questions.question: Persons whose austerity is meager can hardly obtain the service of whom, who are progressing on the path back to the Vaikunthas?
questions.explanation: "Persons whose austerity is meager can hardly obtain the service of the pure devotees who are progressing on the path back to the kingdom of Godhead, the Vaikunthas." (SB 3.7.20)

questions.question: The purusa incarnation lying on the Causal Ocean is called the original purusa; in His virat form He has how many legs and hands?
questions.explanation: "...and in His virat form, in whom all the planets and their inhabitants live, He has many thousands of legs and hands." (SB 3.7.22)

questions.question: Vidura requested Maitreya to describe how which leader of all the demigods decided to establish the various Manus, the heads of the ages?
questions.explanation: "...please describe how the leader of all the demigods, namely the Prajapati, Brahma, decided to establish the various Manus, the heads of the ages." (SB 3.7.25)

questions.question: Which three incarnations of the material modes of nature did Vidura ask Maitreya to describe?
questions.explanation: "Please also describe the incarnations of the material modes of nature -- Brahma, Visnu and Mahesvara..." (SB 3.7.28)

questions.question: Vidura also inquired about the regulations for offering respects to the forefathers and the creation of which planet?
questions.explanation: "Please also describe the regulations for offering respects to the forefathers, the creation of the Pitrloka, the time schedule in the planets..." (SB 3.7.33)

questions.question: Because the Personality of Godhead is the father of all religion, Vidura asked Maitreya to describe what?

options.text: How He can be completely satisfied
How He sleeps in the water

questions.explanation: "...kindly describe how He can be completely satisfied." (SB 3.7.35)

questions.question: Vidura said that Maitreya's answers would grant immunity from all material miseries, and that such charity is greater than what?

options.text: All Vedic charities, sacrifices, penances, etc.

questions.explanation: "Such charity is greater than all Vedic charities, sacrifices, penances, etc." (SB 3.7.41)

questions.question: Being infused by Vidura, what did the chief of the sages begin to narrate?

options.text: The descriptive explanation of the Puranas
The history of the Kuru dynasty

questions.explanation: "...began to narrate the descriptive explanation of the Puranas, being so infused by Vidura." (SB 3.7.42)

topics.name: Chapter 8: Manifestation of Brahma from Garbhodakasayi Visnu

questions.question: Maitreya said that the royal dynasty of which king is worthy to serve the pure devotees, the family in which Vidura was born?
questions.explanation: "The royal dynasty of King Puru is worthy to serve the pure devotees because all the descendants of that family are devoted to the Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.8.1)

questions.question: The Bhagavata Purana was directly spoken to the great sages by whom?
questions.explanation: "Let me now begin speaking on the Bhagavata Purana, which was directly spoken to the great sages by the Personality of Godhead..." (SB 3.8.2)

questions.question: From whom did Sanat-kumara, chief of the boy-saints, inquire about the truths regarding Vasudeva?

options.text: Lord Sankarsana, who is seated at the bottom of the universe

questions.explanation: "...Sanat-kumara, the chief of the boy-saints, accompanied by other great sages, inquired exactly like you about the truths regarding Vasudeva, the Supreme, from Lord Sankarsana, who is seated at the bottom of the universe." (SB 3.8.3)

questions.question: Upon whom was Lord Sankarsana meditating, whom the learned esteem as Lord Vasudeva?
questions.explanation: "At that time Lord Sankarsana was meditating upon His Supreme Lord, whom the learned esteem as Lord Vasudeva..." (SB 3.8.4)

questions.question: After Sankarsana spoke Srimad-Bhagavatam to Sanat-kumara, Sanat-kumara explained it when inquired of by which muni?
questions.explanation: "Sanat-kumara also, in his turn, when inquired of by Sankhyayana Muni, explained Srimad-Bhagavatam as he had heard it from Sankarsana." (SB 3.8.7)

questions.question: When the great sage Sankhyayana was describing the glories of the Lord, which two personalities heard him?
questions.explanation: "...it so happened that my spiritual master, Parasara, and Brhaspati both heard him." (SB 3.8.8)

questions.question: When the three worlds were submerged in water, Garbhodakasayi Visnu was lying alone on which bedstead?
questions.explanation: "...Garbhodakasayi Visnu was alone, lying on His bedstead, the great snake Ananta..." (SB 3.8.10)

questions.question: For how long did the Lord lie down in His internal potency, appearing to sleep within the water?

options.text: A thousand cycles of four yugas

questions.explanation: "The Lord lay down for a thousand cycles of four yugas in His internal potency, and by His external energy He appeared to be sleeping within the water." (SB 3.8.12)

questions.question: As the living entities came out for development of their fruitive activities, the Lord saw His transcendental body as what color?
questions.explanation: "...He saw His transcendental body as bluish." (SB 3.8.12)

questions.question: The subtle form of creation, agitated by the mode of passion, pierced through which part of the Lord?
questions.explanation: "The subtle subject matter of creation, on which the Lord's attention was fixed, was agitated by the material mode of passion, and thus the subtle form of creation pierced through His abdomen." (SB 3.8.13)

questions.question: The sum total form of fruitive activity took the shape of what, generated from the Personality of Visnu?

options.text: The bud of a lotus flower

questions.explanation: "Piercing through, this sum total form of the fruitive activity of the living entities took the shape of the bud of a lotus flower generated from the Personality of Visnu..." (SB 3.8.14)

questions.question: Who was generated when the universal lotus flower was impregnated with all the modes of material nature?

options.text: The personality of Vedic wisdom, the self-born

questions.explanation: "...the personality of Vedic wisdom, whom we call the self-born, was generated." (SB 3.8.15)

questions.question: How did Brahma achieve four heads while moving his eyes in all directions?

options.text: In terms of the four directions

questions.explanation: "He therefore circumambulated all of space, and while moving his eyes in all directions he achieved four heads in terms of the four directions." (SB 3.8.16)

questions.question: Searching to trace the origin of the lotus, Brahma entered the water through what?

options.text: The channel of the stem of the lotus

questions.explanation: "Lord Brahma, thus contemplating, entered the water through the channel of the stem of the lotus." (SB 3.8.19)

questions.question: Unable to trace the root, Brahma came back to the top of the lotus and finally realized the Supreme Lord by what means?

options.text: By looking into the stem of the lotus
By concentrating his mind on the Supreme Lord

questions.explanation: "Thus, controlling all objectives, he concentrated his mind on the Supreme Lord." (SB 3.8.21)

questions.question: At the end of how many years of Brahma's meditation could he see the Supreme within his own heart?
questions.explanation: "At the end of Brahma's one hundred years, when his meditation was complete, he developed the required knowledge, and as a result he could see in his heart the Supreme within himself..." (SB 3.8.22)

questions.question: On whose body, like a lotuslike white bedstead, did Brahma see the Personality of Godhead lying alone on the water?
questions.explanation: "Brahma could see that on the water there was a gigantic lotuslike white bedstead, the body of Sesa-naga, on which the Personality of Godhead was lying alone." (SB 3.8.23)

questions.question: The gold on the summit of the coral mountain was mocked by what feature of the Lord?
questions.explanation: "There is gold on the summit of the mountain, but the Lord's helmet, bedecked with jewels, mocked it." (SB 3.8.24)

questions.question: Brahma saw the Lord's chest decorated with which marking and a necklace of unlimited value?
questions.explanation: "His chest was decorated with the srivatsa marking and a necklace of unlimited value." (SB 3.8.28)

questions.question: After being surcharged with the mode of passion and inclined to create, Brahma offered prayers after seeing how many causes of creation?
questions.explanation: "...after seeing the five causes of creation indicated by the Personality of Godhead, he began to offer his respectful prayers on the path of the creative mentality." (SB 3.8.33)

topics.name: Chapter 9: Brahma's Prayers for Creative Energy

questions.question: After how long did Lord Brahma say he had come to know about the Lord?
questions.explanation: "O my Lord, today, after many, many years of penance, I have come to know about You." (SB 3.9.1)

questions.question: Brahma said the Lord's form is eternally freed from material contamination and has advented to show mercy to the devotees as a manifestation of what?
questions.explanation: "The form which I see is eternally freed from material contamination and has advented to show mercy to the devotees as a manifestation of internal potency." (SB 3.9.2)

questions.question: Why does Brahma surrender unto the Lord, who is the cause of the cosmic manifestation?

options.text: Because the Lord is untouched by matter
Because the Lord rewards His devotees
Because the Lord controls the demigods

questions.explanation: "I surrender unto You because whereas I am proud of my material body and senses, Your Lordship is the cause of the cosmic manifestation and yet You are untouched by matter." (SB 3.9.3)

questions.question: According to Brahma, who neglect the Lord's personal form because of speculating on material topics?

options.text: Those who are destined to be dispatched to the path of hell

questions.explanation: "Those who are destined to be dispatched to the path of hell neglect Your personal form because of speculating on material topics." (SB 3.9.4)

questions.question: Brahma considers the common people unfortunate because they are bereft of the all-auspicious performance of what?

options.text: Chanting and hearing about the Lord's transcendental activities

questions.explanation: "...persons who are bereft of the all-auspicious performance of chanting and hearing about Your transcendental activities are certainly unfortunate and are also bereft of good sense." (SB 3.9.7)

questions.question: Brahma takes pity on poor creatures who are overwhelmed by which urges, in addition to hunger, thirst and severe cold?

options.text: Strong sex urges and indefatigable anger

questions.explanation: "...and overwhelmed by strong sex urges and indefatigable anger. I take pity on them, and I am very much aggrieved for them." (SB 3.9.8)

questions.question: According to Brahma, even great sages must rotate in this material world if they are against what?
questions.explanation: "Even great sages, if they are against Your transcendental topics, must rotate in this material world." (SB 3.9.10)

questions.question: By what process do the Lord's devotees see Him, so that their hearts become cleansed and He takes His seat there?

options.text: Through the eyes by Deity worship
Through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing

questions.explanation: "O my Lord, Your devotees can see You through the ears by the process of bona fide hearing, and thus their hearts become cleansed, and You take Your seat there." (SB 3.9.11)

questions.question: Brahma said the Lord is not very much satisfied by the worship of whom, who are full of material hankerings?
questions.explanation: "My Lord, You are not very much satisfied by the worship of the demigods, who arrange for Your worship very pompously, with various paraphernalia, but who are full of material hankerings." (SB 3.9.12)

questions.question: Brahma said the tree of planetary systems has grown by first penetrating the material nature in three trunks. Which three?

options.text: Brahma, Siva and the Almighty Lord
Vishnu, Siva and the goddess Kali

questions.explanation: "This tree has grown by first penetrating the material nature in three trunks -- as me, Siva and You, the Almighty -- for creation, maintenance and dissolution..." (SB 3.9.16)

questions.question: To whom does Brahma offer obeisances after stating that the foolish work of people will be cut to pieces?

options.text: Him who acts as eternal time

questions.explanation: "I therefore offer my obeisances unto Him who acts as eternal time." (SB 3.9.17)

questions.question: Brahma said he is situated in an abode which will continue to exist for a time duration of how many parardhas?
questions.explanation: "Although I am situated in an abode which will continue to exist for a time duration of two parardhas..." (SB 3.9.18)

questions.question: While the Lord enjoys the pleasure of sleeping on the bed of snakes in the water of devastation, what is stationed within His abdomen?
questions.explanation: "At that time, all the universal planets are stationed within Your abdomen." (SB 3.9.20)

questions.question: Brahma prays to be empowered, as before, with what, declaring himself one of the surrendered souls dear to the Lord?
questions.explanation: "May He be merciful towards me so that I, as before, may be empowered with the introspection to create..." (SB 3.9.22)

questions.question: The Lord's activities are always enacted through His internal potency, known by what name?

options.text: Rama, or the goddess of fortune

questions.explanation: "His activities are always enacted through His internal potency, Rama, or the goddess of fortune." (SB 3.9.23)

questions.question: After Brahma prayed and became silent, the Lord understood Brahma was anxious about what?

options.text: The planning and construction of the different planetary systems

questions.explanation: "The Lord saw that Brahma was very anxious about the planning and construction of the different planetary systems and was depressed upon seeing the devastating water." (SB 3.9.27-28)

questions.question: The Supreme Personality of Godhead told Brahma not to be depressed or anxious, because what he was begging had been done when?

options.text: It has already been granted before
It will be granted in the next millennium
It is granted at the time of annihilation
It is granted by the demigods

questions.explanation: "What you are begging from Me has already been granted before." (SB 3.9.29)

questions.question: The Lord told Brahma that he would see the Lord in all living entities and over the universe, just as fire is situated where?
questions.explanation: "You will see Me in all living entities as well as all over the universe, just as fire is situated in wood." (SB 3.9.32)

questions.question: The Lord assured Brahma that because his mind is always fixed on Him, which mode will never encroach upon him even while generating progeny?
questions.explanation: "...even though you will be engaged in generating various progeny the vicious mode of passion will never encroach upon you." (SB 3.9.35)

questions.question: After instructing Brahma to expand the creation, in which personal form did the primeval Lord disappear?
questions.explanation: "...the primeval Lord, the Personality of Godhead in His personal form as Narayana, disappeared." (SB 3.9.44)

topics.name: Chapter 10: Divisions of the Creation

questions.question: Vidura asked how Brahma created the bodies of the living entities after whose disappearance?
questions.explanation: "...please let me know how Brahma, the grandfather of the planetary inhabitants, created the bodies of the living entities from his own body and mind after the disappearance of the Supreme Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.10.1)

questions.question: Who replied to Vidura's questions, narrating that everything was in his heart?
questions.explanation: "...the great sage Maitreya Muni, thus hearing from Vidura, felt very much enlivened. Everything was in his heart, and thus he began to reply to the questions one after another." (SB 3.10.3)

questions.question: For how long did Brahma engage in penances and devotional service, as advised by the Personality of Godhead?
questions.explanation: "...Brahma thus engaged himself in penances for one hundred celestial years, as advised by the Personality of Godhead, and applied himself in devotional service to the Lord." (SB 3.10.4)

questions.question: What did Brahma do with the strong, violent wind and the water that were making the lotus tremble?

options.text: He drank the wind completely, along with the water
He stopped it with his mind
He prayed for it to stop

questions.explanation: "Long penance and transcendental knowledge of self-realization had matured Brahma in practical knowledge, and thus he drank the wind completely, along with the water." (SB 3.10.6)

questions.question: After entering the whorl of the lotus, Brahma divided it into three divisions of worlds and later into how many divisions?
questions.explanation: "...he divided it into three divisions of worlds and later into fourteen divisions." (SB 3.10.8)

questions.question: Why is Lord Brahma described as the most exalted personality in the universe?

options.text: Because of his causeless devotional service unto the Lord in mature transcendental knowledge
Because he was born from the lotus

questions.explanation: "Lord Brahma is the most exalted personality in the universe because of his causeless devotional service unto the Lord in mature transcendental knowledge." (SB 3.10.9)

questions.question: What is described as the primeval source of the interactions of the three modes of material nature?
questions.explanation: "Eternal time is the primeval source of the interactions of the three modes of material nature." (SB 3.10.11)

questions.question: Besides the nine kinds of creation, how many kinds of annihilations are there due to eternal time, the material elements and the quality of work?
questions.explanation: "There are three kinds of annihilations due to eternal time, the material elements and the quality of one's work." (SB 3.10.14)

questions.question: Of the nine creations, what is the first one?

options.text: The creation of the false ego
The creation of the mahat-tattva, or the sum total of the material ingredients
The creation of the controlling deities

questions.explanation: "Of the nine creations, the first one is the creation of the mahat-tattva, or the sum total of the material ingredients, wherein the modes interact due to the presence of the Supreme Lord." (SB 3.10.15)

questions.question: In which creation are the sense perceptions created, from which the elements are generated?
questions.explanation: "The sense perceptions are created in the third creation, and from these the elements are generated." (SB 3.10.16)

questions.question: The sixth creation is described as what?

options.text: The creation of the controlling deities
The ignorant darkness of the living entity, by which the master acts as a fool
The creation of knowledge and working capacity
The creation of the immovable entities

questions.explanation: "The sixth creation is the ignorant darkness of the living entity, by which the master acts as a fool." (SB 3.10.17)

questions.question: Brahma is described as an incarnation of which mode, having a brain like that of the Personality of Godhead in the matter of creation?
questions.explanation: "...the creations by Brahma, who is an incarnation of the mode of passion and who, in the matter of creation, has a brain like that of the Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.10.18)

questions.question: The seventh creation is that of the immovable entities, which are of how many kinds?
questions.explanation: "The seventh creation is that of the immovable entities, which are of six kinds..." (SB 3.10.19)

questions.question: The eighth creation is that of the lower species of life, numbering how many varieties?
questions.explanation: "The eighth creation is that of the lower species of life, and they are of different varieties, numbering twenty-eight." (SB 3.10.21)

questions.question: How do the lower species of the eighth creation know their desirables?
questions.explanation: "They know their desirables by smell, but are unable to remember anything within the heart." (SB 3.10.21)

questions.question: The horse, mule, ass, gaura, sarabha bison and wild cow are described as animals with how many hooves?
questions.explanation: "The horse, mule, ass, gaura, sarabha bison and wild cow all have only one hoof." (SB 3.10.23)

questions.question: The dog, jackal, tiger, monkey, elephant and others are known as panca-nakhas because they have what?
questions.explanation: "The dog, jackal, tiger, fox, cat, rabbit, sajaru, lion, monkey, elephant, tortoise, alligator, gosapa, etc., all have five nails in their claws." (SB 3.10.24)

questions.question: Which creation is that of the human beings, who are of one species and stock their eatables in the belly?
questions.explanation: "The creation of the human beings, who are of one species only and who stock their eatables in the belly, is the ninth in the rotation." (SB 3.10.26)

questions.question: In the human race, which mode is very prominent?
questions.explanation: "In the human race, the mode of passion is very prominent." (SB 3.10.26)

questions.question: The creation of the demigods, the tenth creation, is of how many varieties?
questions.explanation: "The creation of the demigods is of eight varieties..." (SB 3.10.28-29)

topics.name: Chapter 11: Calculation of Time, from the Atom

questions.question: What is the name given to the material manifestation's ultimate particle, which is indivisible and not formed into a body?
questions.explanation: "The material manifestation's ultimate particle, which is indivisible and not formed into a body, is called the atom." (SB 3.11.1)

questions.question: Atoms are the ultimate state of what?
questions.explanation: "Atoms are the ultimate state of the manifest universe." (SB 3.11.2)

questions.question: Time is described as the potency of which Personality of Godhead?
questions.explanation: "Time is the potency of the almighty Personality of Godhead, Hari, who controls all physical movement although He is not visible in the physical world." (SB 3.11.3)

questions.question: The hexatom, the combination of three double atoms, is visible in what?

options.text: The sunshine entering through holes of a window screen

questions.explanation: "This hexatom is visible in the sunshine which enters through the holes of a window screen." (SB 3.11.5)

questions.question: One hundred trutis make one of what unit?
questions.explanation: "The time duration needed for the integration of three trasarenus is called a truti, and one hundred trutis make one vedha." (SB 3.11.6)

questions.question: Fifteen kasthas make one of what unit?
questions.explanation: "...five ksanas combined together make one kastha, and fifteen kasthas make one laghu." (SB 3.11.7)

questions.question: How many dandas (nadikas) make one muhurta?
questions.explanation: "Two dandas make one muhurta..." (SB 3.11.8)

questions.question: How many fortnights are there in a month?
questions.explanation: "...and there are two fortnights, white and black, in a month." (SB 3.11.10)

questions.question: One complete month (two fortnights) is equal to one complete day and night for which planets?
questions.explanation: "The aggregate of two fortnights is one month, and that period is one complete day and night for the Pita planets." (SB 3.11.11)

questions.question: A combination of how many day and night of the demigods forms one complete calendar year for a human being?
questions.explanation: "Two solar movements make one day and night of the demigods, and that combination of day and night is one complete calendar year for the human being." (SB 3.11.12)

questions.question: How often should everyone offer respects to the sun with all ingredients of worship?
questions.explanation: "...and therefore everyone should offer him respects once every five years with all ingredients of worship." (SB 3.11.15)

questions.question: The aggregate number of years of all four millenniums combined is equal to how many thousand years of the demigods?
questions.explanation: "The aggregate number of years of all of these combined is equal to twelve thousand years of the demigods." (SB 3.11.18)

questions.question: The duration of the Satya millennium equals how many years of the demigods?
questions.explanation: "The duration of the Satya millennium equals 4,800 years of the years of the demigods..." (SB 3.11.19)

questions.question: The four yugas multiplied by one thousand comprise one of what for the planet of Brahma?
questions.explanation: "...the four yugas multiplied by one thousand comprise one day on the planet of Brahma." (SB 3.11.22)

questions.question: The three worlds continue to exist during Brahma's day through the life durations of how many consecutive Manus?
questions.explanation: "...and they continue to exist through the life durations of fourteen consecutive Manus, or fathers of mankind." (SB 3.11.23)

questions.question: Each Manu enjoys a life of a little more than how many sets of four millenniums?
questions.explanation: "Each and every Manu enjoys a life of a little more than seventy-one sets of four millenniums." (SB 3.11.24)

questions.question: The devastation at the end of Brahma's day takes place due to fire emanating from the mouth of whom?
questions.explanation: "The devastation takes place due to the fire emanating from the mouth of Sankarsana..." (SB 3.11.30)

questions.question: Which half of Brahma's life is described as currently being in progress?
questions.explanation: "The first half of the duration of Brahma's life is already over, and the second half is now current." (SB 3.11.34)

questions.question: Why is the Varaha millennium so named?

options.text: The Personality of Godhead appeared as the hog incarnation

questions.explanation: "...the Varaha millennium because the Personality of Godhead appeared in that millennium as the hog incarnation." (SB 3.11.37)

questions.question: The duration of the two parts of Brahma's entire life equals what for the Supreme Personality of Godhead?
questions.explanation: "The duration of the two parts of Brahma's life, as above mentioned, is calculated to be equal to one nimesa [less than a second] for the Supreme Personality of Godhead..." (SB 3.11.38)

questions.question: How much thicker is each layer of elements covering the universes than the one before?
questions.explanation: "The layers or elements covering the universes are each ten times thicker than the one before..." (SB 3.11.41)

topics.name: Chapter 12: Creation of the Kumaras and Others

questions.question: Whose creation does Maitreya describe in this chapter as the reservoir of all Vedic knowledge?
questions.explanation: "Now you can hear from me about the creation of Brahma, the reservoir of all Vedic knowledge." (SB 3.12.1)

questions.question: What did Brahma first create at the beginning?

options.text: The nescient engagements like self-deception and anger

questions.explanation: "Brahma first created the nescient engagements like self-deception, the sense of death, anger after frustration, the sense of false ownership, and the illusory bodily conception..." (SB 3.12.2)

questions.question: What were the names of the four great sages Brahma created in the beginning?
questions.explanation: "In the beginning, Brahma created four great sages named Sanaka, Sananda, Sanatana and Sanat-kumara." (SB 3.12.4)

questions.question: Why did the four Kumaras refuse Brahma's order to generate progeny?

options.text: Being attached to Vasudeva, they aimed at liberation

questions.explanation: "But due to their being attached to Vasudeva, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, they aimed at liberation, and therefore they expressed their unwillingness." (SB 3.12.5)

questions.question: From where did the blue and red child generated from Brahma's anger come out?
questions.explanation: "Although he tried to curb his anger, it came out from between his eyebrows, and a child mixed blue and red was immediately generated." (SB 3.12.7)

questions.question: By what name did Brahma say the crying boy would be called by all people?
questions.explanation: "...you shall be called by the name Rudra by all people because you have so anxiously cried." (SB 3.12.10)

questions.question: Besides Rudra, how many other names did Brahma give to the boy?
questions.explanation: "My dear boy Rudra, you have eleven other names: Manyu, Manu, Mahinasa, Mahan, Siva, Rtadhvaja, Ugrareta, Bhava, Kala, Vamadeva and Dhrtavrata." (SB 3.12.12)

questions.question: How many wives, called the Rudranis, did Rudra have?
questions.explanation: "O Rudra, you also have eleven wives, called the Rudranis..." (SB 3.12.13)

questions.question: Why did Brahma become afraid when Rudra's offspring assembled together?

options.text: They attempted to devour the entire universe

questions.explanation: "...when they assembled together they attempted to devour the entire universe. When Brahma, the father of the living entities, saw this, he became afraid of the situation." (SB 3.12.16)

questions.question: After being ordered by Brahma to perform penance, what did Rudra do?

options.text: He entered the forest to perform austere penances
He went to the heavenly planets

questions.explanation: "Addressing him with words of assent, he entered the forest to perform austere penances." (SB 3.12.20)

questions.question: How many sons did Brahma beget for the extension of the generations?
questions.explanation: "...thought of generating living entities and begot ten sons for the extension of the generations." (SB 3.12.21)

questions.question: From which part of Brahma was Narada born?
questions.explanation: "Narada was born from the deliberation of Brahma, which is the best part of the body." (SB 3.12.23)

questions.question: From which part of Brahma was religion manifested?
questions.explanation: "Religion was manifested from the breast of Brahma, wherein is seated the Supreme Personality of Godhead Narayana..." (SB 3.12.25)

questions.question: Sage Kardama, husband of Devahuti, was manifested from what?
questions.explanation: "Sage Kardama, husband of the great Devahuti, was manifested from the shadow of Brahma." (SB 3.12.27)

questions.question: What was the name of Brahma's daughter who attracted his mind toward sex?
questions.explanation: "...we have heard that Brahma had a daughter named Vak who was born from his body and who attracted his mind toward sex..." (SB 3.12.28)

questions.question: After the sages rebuked him, what did the ashamed Brahma do with the body he had accepted?

options.text: He at once gave it up

questions.explanation: "...became very much ashamed and at once gave up the body he had accepted." (SB 3.12.33)

questions.question: When Brahma was thinking of how to create the worlds, what became manifested from his four mouths?
questions.explanation: "...the four Vedas, which contain all varieties of knowledge, became manifested from his four mouths." (SB 3.12.34)

questions.question: Beginning from which face of Brahma did the four Vedas gradually become manifest?
questions.explanation: "Beginning from the front face of Brahma, gradually the four Vedas — Rk, Yajur, Sama and Atharva — became manifest." (SB 3.12.37)

questions.question: From which mouth of Brahma did the different varieties of fire sacrifices become manifested?
questions.explanation: "All the different varieties of fire sacrifices...became manifested from the eastern mouth of Brahma." (SB 3.12.40)

questions.question: The male and female forms generated from Brahma's body became known as Manu Svayambhuva and which queen?
questions.explanation: "...the one who had the male form became known as the Manu named Svayambhuva, and the woman became known as Satarupa, the queen of the great soul Manu." (SB 3.12.54)

questions.question: How many children did Manu beget in Satarupa?
questions.explanation: "...he [Manu] begot in Satarupa five children — two sons, Priyavrata and Uttanapada, and three daughters, Akuti, Devahuti and Prasuti." (SB 3.12.56)

topics.name: Chapter 13: The Appearance of Lord Varaha

questions.question: On whose lap was Lord Krishna pleased to place His lotus feet because that person was very meek and gentle?
questions.explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, Sri Krishna, was pleased to place His lotus feet on the lap of Vidura because Vidura was very meek and gentle." (SB 3.13.5)

questions.question: What did Brahma ask Manu to do to render the best service unto him?

options.text: Beget qualified children and rule the world in devotional service
Travel to all the holy places

questions.explanation: "...I ask you to beget children qualified like yourself in the womb of your wife. Rule the world in pursuance of the principles of devotional service unto the Supreme Personality of Godhead..." (SB 3.13.11)

questions.question: What problem with the earth did Manu ask Brahma to solve so that it could be the dwelling place for all living entities?

options.text: It was merged in the great water
It was floating in the sky

questions.explanation: "...please attempt to lift the earth, which is merged in the great water, because it is the dwelling place for all the living entities." (SB 3.13.15)

questions.question: From which part of Brahma did the small form of a boar come out?
questions.explanation: "...all of a sudden, while Brahma was engaged in thinking, a small form of a boar came out of his nostril." (SB 3.13.18)

questions.question: How big was the boar when it first came out of Brahma's nostril?

options.text: Not more than the upper portion of a thumb

questions.explanation: "The measurement of the creature was not more than the upper portion of a thumb." (SB 3.13.18)

questions.question: As Brahma watched, the boar quickly became situated in the sky as gigantic as what?
questions.explanation: "...that boar became situated in the sky in a wonderful manifestation as gigantic as a great elephant." (SB 3.13.19)

questions.question: How did the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vishnu, in the boar form enliven Brahma and the brahmanas?

options.text: By roaring tumultuously like a great mountain

questions.explanation: "While Brahma was deliberating with his sons, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vishnu, roared tumultuously like a great mountain." (SB 3.13.23)

questions.question: When Lord Boar dived into the water like a giant mountain, what appeared as the arms of the ocean?
questions.explanation: "...Lord Boar divided the middle of the ocean, and two high waves appeared as the arms of the ocean..." (SB 3.13.29)

questions.question: How did Lord Boar get the earth out of the water?

options.text: He carried it in His arms
He took it on His tusks
He pushed it with His hooves
He balanced it on His head

questions.explanation: "Lord Boar very easily took the earth on His tusks and got it out of the water." (SB 3.13.31)

questions.question: While lifting the earth, whom did Lord Boar immediately kill?
questions.explanation: "...His anger glowing like the Sudarsana wheel, He immediately killed the demon [Hiranyaksa], although he tried to fight with the Lord." (SB 3.13.31)

questions.question: What happened to the cheeks and tongue of the Lord after He killed the demon within the water?

options.text: They became smeared with the blood of the demon
