questions.explanation: "The cheeks and tongue of the Lord became smeared with the blood of the demon, just as an elephant becomes reddish from digging in the purple earth." (SB 3.13.32)

questions.question: What complexion did the Lord assume while suspending the earth on His tusks like an elephant?

options.text: A bluish complexion like that of a tamala tree

questions.explanation: "He assumed a bluish complexion like that of a tamala tree..." (SB 3.13.33)

questions.question: According to the sages' prayers, what are submerged in the hair holes of Lord Boar's body?
questions.explanation: "...and in the hair holes of Your body the oceans are submerged." (SB 3.13.34)

questions.question: In the prayers, what are described as plates of sacrifice of the Lord?

options.text: The tongue, nostril, belly and ears

questions.explanation: "O Lord, Your tongue is a plate of sacrifice, Your nostril is another plate of sacrifice, in Your belly is the eating plate of sacrifice, and another plate of sacrifice is the holes of Your ears." (SB 3.13.36)

questions.question: According to the prayers, the Lord's neck is the place for what?
questions.explanation: "Your neck is the place for three desires, and Your tusks are the result of initiation and the end of all desires." (SB 3.13.37)

questions.question: The earth lifted on the Lord's tusks is compared to what beautiful object?

options.text: A lotus flower sustained by an infuriated elephant

questions.explanation: "...the earth with its mountains, which You have lifted with Your tusks, is situated as beautifully as a lotus flower with leaves sustained by an infuriated elephant just coming out of the water." (SB 3.13.40)

questions.question: In the prayers, the earth is described as the Lord's what?
questions.explanation: "...this earth is Your wife, and You are the supreme father." (SB 3.13.42)

questions.question: How were the sages of the Jana, Tapas and Satya lokas purified by the Lord?

options.text: By the drops of water sprinkled from His shoulder hairs

questions.explanation: "...but still we have been purified by the drops of water sprinkled from Your shoulder hairs by the shaking of Your body." (SB 3.13.44)

questions.question: After raising the earth and placing it afloat on the water, what did Lord Vishnu do?

options.text: He returned to His own abode

questions.explanation: "...He returned to His own abode." (SB 3.13.47)

questions.question: What is the benefit of hearing and describing the narration of Lord Boar in a devotional service attitude?

options.text: The Lord, who is within the heart of everyone, is very pleased

questions.explanation: "If one hears and describes in a devotional service attitude this auspicious narration of Lord Boar, which is worthy of description, the Lord, who is within the heart of everyone, is very pleased." (SB 3.13.48)

topics.name: Chapter 14: Pregnancy of Diti in the Evening

questions.question: After hearing about which incarnation of the Lord did Vidura beg Maitreya to narrate further transcendental activities?
questions.explanation: "After hearing from the great sage Maitreya about the Lord's incarnation as Varaha, Vidura, who had taken a vow, begged him with folded hands to please narrate further transcendental activities of the Lord..." (SB 3.14.1)

questions.question: According to Vidura, who was the original demon slain by Lord Boar?
questions.explanation: "I have heard by disciplic succession that Hiranyaksa, the original demon, was slain by the same form of sacrifices, the Personality of Godhead [Lord Boar]." (SB 3.14.2)

questions.question: The son of King Uttanapada, who ascended to the abode of the Lord placing his feet over the head of death, was who?
questions.explanation: "...the son of King Uttanapada [Dhruva] was enlightened regarding the Personality of Godhead, and he ascended to the abode of the Lord, placing his feet over the head of death." (SB 3.14.6)

questions.question: Who was Diti's father?
questions.explanation: "Diti, daughter of Daksa, being afflicted with sex desire, begged her husband, Kasyapa, the son of Marici, to have intercourse with her..." (SB 3.14.8)

questions.question: At what time of day did Diti beg Kasyapa to have intercourse with her in order to beget a child?
questions.explanation: "...begged her husband, Kasyapa, the son of Marici, to have intercourse with her in the evening in order to beget a child." (SB 3.14.8)

questions.question: When Diti approached Kasyapa, what was the sage doing?

options.text: Sitting in trance after offering oblations to Vishnu
Performing a fire sacrifice for the demigods

questions.explanation: "The sun was setting, and the sage was sitting in trance after offering oblations to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vishnu, whose tongue is the sacrificial fire." (SB 3.14.9)

questions.question: How many of his daughters did Daksa hand over to Kasyapa?
questions.explanation: "Our well-wishing father, Daksa...handed over thirteen of his daughters unto you, and since then we have all been faithful." (SB 3.14.14)

questions.question: Kasyapa compared crossing the dangerous situation of the material ocean to crossing the ocean with what?
questions.explanation: "As one can cross over the ocean with seagoing vessels, one can cross the dangerous situation of the material ocean by living with a wife." (SB 3.14.18)

questions.question: Why did Kasyapa describe the particular evening time as most inauspicious?

options.text: Because the horrible-looking ghosts and companions of the lord of the ghosts are visible
Because the Vedas forbade all activity

questions.explanation: "This particular time is most inauspicious because at this time the horrible-looking ghosts and constant companions of the lord of the ghosts are visible." (SB 3.14.23)

questions.question: Who travels at that evening time on the back of his bull carrier, accompanied by ghosts?
questions.explanation: "Lord Siva, the king of the ghosts, sitting on the back of his bull carrier, travels at this time, accompanied by ghosts who follow him for their welfare." (SB 3.14.24)

questions.question: What is the relationship of Lord Siva to Diti's husband Kasyapa?

options.text: He is the younger brother of her husband

questions.explanation: "He is the younger brother of your husband, and he sees with his three eyes." (SB 3.14.25)

questions.question: When Diti was pressed by Cupid, what did she do despite her husband's words?

options.text: She caught hold of the clothing of the great brahmana sage

questions.explanation: "...she was pressed by Cupid for sexual satisfaction. She caught hold of the clothing of the great brahmana sage, just like a shameless public prostitute." (SB 3.14.30)

questions.question: After realizing her fault, Diti begged Kasyapa to bless her so that her embryo would not be killed by whom?
questions.explanation: "My dear brahmana, kindly see that my embryo is not killed by Lord Siva, the lord of all living entities, because of the great offense I have committed against him." (SB 3.14.34)

questions.question: Diti described Lord Siva as her brother-in-law because he is the husband of which sister?
questions.explanation: "Let him be pleased with us, since he is my brother-in-law, the husband of my sister Sati." (SB 3.14.36)

questions.question: How many contemptuous sons did Kasyapa foretell would be born of Diti's condemned womb?
questions.explanation: "O haughty one, you will have two contemptuous sons born of your condemned womb." (SB 3.14.39)

questions.question: What did Kasyapa foretell that Diti's sons would do to the three worlds?

options.text: Cause constant lamentation to all the three worlds

questions.explanation: "Unlucky woman, they will cause constant lamentation to all the three worlds!" (SB 3.14.39)

questions.question: According to Kasyapa, who would descend to kill Diti's demoniac sons?
questions.explanation: "...the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the well-wisher of all living entities, will descend and kill them, just as Indra smashes the mountains with his thunderbolts." (SB 3.14.41)

questions.question: How did Diti react to learning her sons would be killed by the Personality of Godhead with His Sudarsana weapon?
questions.explanation: "It is very good that my sons will be magnanimously killed by the arms of the Personality of Godhead with His Sudarsana weapon." (SB 3.14.42)

questions.question: Kasyapa foretold that which grandson of Diti (son of Hiranyakasipu) would be an approved devotee of the Lord?
questions.explanation: "...one of the sons [Prahlada] of your son [Hiranyakasipu] will be an approved devotee of the Lord, and his fame will be broadcast equally with that of the Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.14.44-45)

questions.question: What did Kasyapa say Diti's grandson would do after quitting the material world?
questions.explanation: "Due to matured devotional service, he will certainly be situated in transcendental ecstasy and will enter the spiritual sky after quitting this material world." (SB 3.14.48)

topics.name: Chapter 15: Description of the Kingdom of God

questions.question: For how many years did Diti continuously bear the powerful semen of Kasyapa Muni in her womb?
questions.explanation: "As such, she continuously bore the powerful semen of Kasyapa Muni, which was meant to give trouble to others, for one hundred years." (SB 3.15.1)

questions.question: What effect did the force of Diti's pregnancy have on the planets?

options.text: It impaired the light of the sun and moon in all the planets

questions.explanation: "By the force of the pregnancy of Diti, the light of the sun and moon was impaired in all the planets..." (SB 3.15.2)

questions.question: When the demigods were disturbed by the darkness, to whom did they appeal for an explanation?

options.text: Brahma, the creator of the universe

questions.explanation: "...the demigods of various planets, being disturbed by that force, asked the creator of the universe, Brahma, 'What is this expansion of darkness in all directions?'" (SB 3.15.2)

questions.question: Whom did Brahma identify as his four mind-born sons and the predecessors of the demigods?
questions.explanation: "My four sons Sanaka, Sanatana, Sanandana and Sanat-kumara, who were born from my mind, are your predecessors." (SB 3.15.12)

questions.question: What are the spiritual planets in the spiritual sky, residence of the Supreme Lord and His pure devotees, called?
questions.explanation: "In the spiritual sky there are spiritual planets known as Vaikunthas, which are the residence of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and His pure devotees..." (SB 3.15.13)

questions.question: In the Vaikuntha planets, the residents are similar in form to whom?
questions.explanation: "In the Vaikuntha planets all the residents are similar in form to the Supreme Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.15.14)

questions.question: What kind of trees grow in the forests of the Vaikuntha planets?
questions.explanation: "In those forests the trees are desire trees, and in all seasons they are filled with flowers and fruits because everything in the Vaikuntha planets is spiritual and personal." (SB 3.15.16)

questions.question: Among all the fragrant flowering plants in Vaikuntha, which is given special preference by the Lord, who garlands Himself with its leaves?
questions.explanation: "...for tulasi is given special preference by the Lord, who garlands Himself with tulasi leaves." (SB 3.15.19)

questions.question: Why do the ladies of the Vaikuntha planets sweep the marble walls bedecked with golden borders?

options.text: To receive the grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead

questions.explanation: "...are sometimes seen sweeping the marble walls, which are bedecked at intervals with golden borders, in order to receive the grace of the Supreme Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.15.21)

questions.question: Where are people thrown who give up the topics of Vaikuntha and take to talk of the material world?

options.text: Into the darkest region of ignorance

questions.explanation: "Those who give up the topics of Vaikuntha and take to talk of the material world are thrown into the darkest region of ignorance." (SB 3.15.23)

questions.question: According to Brahma, what is the special importance of the human form of life?

options.text: One can attain perfect religious truth and knowledge

questions.explanation: "...the human form of life is of such importance that we also desire to have such life, for in the human form one can attain perfect religious truth and knowledge." (SB 3.15.24)

questions.question: Persons whose bodily features change in ecstasy from hearing the Lord's glories are promoted where, even without meditation and austerities?
questions.explanation: "Persons whose bodily features change in ecstasy and who breathe heavily and perspire due to hearing the glories of the Lord are promoted to the kingdom of God..." (SB 3.15.25)

questions.question: After passing through how many entrances of Vaikuntha-puri did the Kumaras reach the gate where the two doorkeepers stood?
questions.explanation: "After passing through the six entrances of Vaikuntha-puri, the Lord's residence, without feeling astonishment at all the decorations, they saw at the seventh gate two shining beings of the same age..." (SB 3.15.27)

questions.question: At which gate were the four sages stopped by the two doorkeepers?
questions.explanation: "...they saw at the seventh gate two shining beings of the same age, armed with maces and adorned with most valuable jewelry..." (SB 3.15.27)

questions.question: Although the four boy-sages were the oldest of all living creatures, how old did they look?
questions.explanation: "The four boy-sages, who had nothing to cover their bodies but the atmosphere, looked only five years old, even though they were the oldest of all living creatures and had realized the truth of the self." (SB 3.15.30)

questions.question: How did the doorkeepers treat the sages when they reached the seventh gate?

options.text: They blocked their way with their staffs, despising their glories
They escorted them to the Lord

questions.explanation: "...they blocked their way with their staffs, despising their glories, although the sages did not deserve such treatment at their hands." (SB 3.15.30)

questions.question: What did the angry sages decide about the two contaminated doorkeepers as a fitting punishment?

options.text: They should be removed to the material world

questions.explanation: "...they are contaminated and should be removed from this place to the material world, where the living entities have three kinds of enemies." (SB 3.15.34)

questions.question: Why could the curse of the brahmanas not be counteracted by the frightened doormen?

options.text: Because a brahmana's curse cannot be counteracted by any kind of weapon

questions.explanation: "...they at once became very much afraid and fell down at the feet of the brahmanas in great anxiety, for a brahmana's curse cannot be counteracted by any kind of weapon." (SB 3.15.35)

questions.question: By what name is the Lord called because of the lotus grown from His navel, who came to the spot accompanied by the goddess of fortune?
questions.explanation: "...the Lord, who is called Padmanabha because of the lotus grown from His navel and who is the delight of the righteous, learned about the insult offered by His own servants to the saints." (SB 3.15.37)

questions.question: On whose shoulder did the Lord rest one of His hands while twirling a lotus with another hand?
questions.explanation: "...He rested one of His hands on the shoulder of Garuda, His carrier, and twirled a lotus with another hand." (SB 3.15.40)

topics.name: Chapter 16: The Two Doorkeepers of Vaikuntha, Jaya and Vijaya, Cursed by the Sages

questions.question: Who narrates the events of this chapter to the sages?
questions.explanation: "Lord Brahma said: After thus congratulating the sages for their nice words, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose abode is in the kingdom of God, spoke as follows." (SB 3.16.1)

questions.question: By what names did the Personality of Godhead identify His two attendants who offended the sages?
questions.explanation: "The Personality of Godhead said: These attendants of Mine, Jaya and Vijaya by name, have committed a great offense against you because of ignoring Me." (SB 3.16.2)

questions.question: What was the Lord's response to the punishment the sages meted out to His doorkeepers?
questions.explanation: "O great sages, I approve of the punishment that you who are devoted to Me have meted out to them." (SB 3.16.3)

questions.question: Whom does the Lord call the highest and most beloved personality?
questions.explanation: "To Me, the brahmana is the highest and most beloved personality." (SB 3.16.4)

questions.question: To what did the Lord compare a servant's wrong act bringing blame upon the master?

options.text: A spot of white leprosy polluting all the skin
A drop of poison in milk

questions.explanation: "A wrong act committed by a servant leads people in general to blame his master, just as a spot of white leprosy on any part of the body pollutes all of the skin." (SB 3.16.5)

questions.question: According to the Lord, what immediately purifies even a candala who eats dog flesh?

options.text: Taking bath in hearing the glorification of the Lord's name

questions.explanation: "Anyone in the entire world, even down to the candala, who lives by cooking and eating the flesh of the dog, is immediately purified if he takes bath in hearing through the ear the glorification of My name, fame, etc." (SB 3.16.6)

questions.question: Why have the Lord's lotus feet become so sacred that they wipe out all sin?

options.text: Because He is the servitor of His devotees

questions.explanation: "The Lord continued: Because I am the servitor of My devotees, My lotus feet have become so sacred that they immediately wipe out all sin..." (SB 3.16.7)

questions.question: Which offering does the Lord relish more than the oblations in the sacrificial fire?

options.text: The delicacies offered to the mouths of the brahmanas

questions.explanation: "I do not enjoy the oblations offered by the sacrificers in the sacrificial fire... with the same relish as I do the delicacies overflowing with ghee which are offered to the mouths of the brahmanas..." (SB 3.16.8)

questions.question: According to the Lord, the water of the Ganges is what?

options.text: The remnant left after His feet are washed

questions.explanation: "I am the master of My unobstructed internal energy, and the water of the Ganges is the remnant left after My feet are washed." (SB 3.16.9)

questions.question: Whom does the Lord describe as His own body?

options.text: The brahmanas, the cows and the defenseless creatures

questions.explanation: "The brahmanas, the cows and the defenseless creatures are My own body." (SB 3.16.10)

questions.question: Whose hearts captivate the Lord, according to verse 11?

options.text: Those who respect the brahmanas even when spoken to harshly

questions.explanation: "On the other hand, they captivate My heart who are gladdened in heart and who... respect the brahmanas, even though the brahmanas utter harsh words." (SB 3.16.11)

questions.question: What favor did the Lord ask the sages to grant regarding His transgressing servants?

options.text: That they be killed at once
That they return to His presence soon and their exile expire before long
That they be sent to Yamaraja

questions.explanation: "I shall therefore deem it a favor done to Me if you order that, although reaping the fruit of their transgression, they may return to My presence soon and the time of their exile from My abode may expire before long." (SB 3.16.12)

questions.question: How did the sages react to the Lord's lovely and illuminating speech?

options.text: Their souls were not satiated with hearing it

questions.explanation: "Even though the sages had been bitten by the serpent of anger, their souls were not satiated with hearing the Lord's lovely and illuminating speech, which was like a series of Vedic hymns." (SB 3.16.13)

questions.question: Through which internal potency did the Lord reveal His multiglories to the four sages?
questions.explanation: "They then spoke as follows to the Lord, who had revealed the multiglories of the Supreme Personality through His internal potency, yoga-maya." (SB 3.16.15)

questions.question: Whom did the sages call the supreme worshipable Deity, even for the brahmanas?
questions.explanation: "Actually You are the supreme worshipable Deity, not only for the gods but for the brahmanas also." (SB 3.16.17)

questions.question: Which goddess does verse 20 describe as waiting upon the Lord, anxious for a place near the tulasi at His feet?
questions.explanation: "The goddess of fortune, Lakshmi, the dust of whose feet is worn on the head by others, waits upon You, as appointed..." (SB 3.16.20)

questions.question: In how many millenniums does the Lord, as personification of all religion, manifest to protect the universe?
questions.explanation: "Therefore You manifest Yourself in three millenniums, and thus You protect this universe, which consists of animate and inanimate beings." (SB 3.16.22)

questions.question: How did the sages respond to whatever punishment the Lord might award them?

options.text: They would accept it without duplicity
They demanded the curse be lifted

questions.explanation: "O Lord, whatever punishment You wish to award to these two innocent persons, or also to us, we shall accept without duplicity." (SB 3.16.25)

questions.question: Into what kind of family did the Lord say Jaya and Vijaya would fall?
questions.explanation: "The Lord replied: O brahmanas, know that the punishment you inflicted on them was originally ordained by Me, and therefore they will fall to a birth in a demoniac family." (SB 3.16.26)

questions.question: By what means, intensified by anger, would Jaya and Vijaya stay united with the Lord and return shortly?
questions.explanation: "But they will be firmly united with Me in thought through mental concentration intensified by anger, and they will return to My presence shortly." (SB 3.16.26)

questions.question: Who had foretold the departure of Jaya and Vijaya from Vaikuntha?
questions.explanation: "This departure from Vaikuntha was foretold by Lakshmi, the goddess of fortune." (SB 3.16.30)

questions.question: Into whose womb did the two doorkeepers of Vaikuntha enter after falling?
questions.explanation: "Those two principal doorkeepers of the Personality of Godhead have now entered the womb of Diti, the powerful semen of Kasyapa Muni having covered them." (SB 3.16.35)

questions.question: Whose desire, according to Brahma, was responsible for the entire arrangement of Jaya and Vijaya's fall?
questions.explanation: "There is no remedy within my power, however, for it is the Lord Himself who desires to do all this." (SB 3.16.36)

topics.name: Chapter 17: Victory of Hiranyaksa in All Directions

questions.question: Who explained to the demigods the cause of the darkness, freeing them from fear?

options.text: Brahma, who was born from Vishnu

questions.explanation: "Sri Maitreya said: The demigods... were freed from all fear upon hearing the cause of the darkness explained by Brahma, who was born from Vishnu." (SB 3.17.1)

questions.question: After how long a pregnancy did Diti bring forth her twin sons?
questions.explanation: "She brought forth twin sons after a full one hundred years of pregnancy." (SB 3.17.2)

questions.question: Which inauspicious planet is named among those that appeared at the demons' birth?
questions.explanation: "Many inauspicious planets like Saturn appeared, along with comets, meteors and thunderbolts." (SB 3.17.4)

questions.question: What did the cows yield in place of milk during the disturbances?
questions.explanation: "Cows, terrified, yielded blood in place of milk, clouds rained pus, the images of the gods in the temples shed tears..." (SB 3.17.13)

questions.question: Who alone were NOT seized with fear at the omens, knowing the secret behind them?

options.text: The four sage sons of Brahma

questions.explanation: "Marking these and many other omens of evil times, everyone but the four sage sons of Brahma... was seized with fear." (SB 3.17.15)

questions.question: To what did the growing bodies of the two demons compare?
questions.explanation: "...they had steel-like frames which began to grow just like two great mountains." (SB 3.17.16)

questions.question: Whom did Kasyapa name the son who was born first?
questions.explanation: "...the one who was born first he named Hiranyaksa, and the one who was first conceived by Diti he named Hiranyakasipu." (SB 3.17.18)

questions.question: Why was Hiranyakasipu unafraid of death from anyone within the three worlds?

options.text: He received a benediction from Lord Brahma

questions.explanation: "The elder child, Hiranyakasipu, was unafraid of death from anyone within the three worlds because he received a benediction from Lord Brahma." (SB 3.17.19)

questions.question: What was Hiranyaksa's chief motive as he traveled the universe with a fighting spirit?

options.text: To satisfy his elder brother Hiranyakasipu

questions.explanation: "His younger brother, Hiranyaksa, was always ready to satisfy his elder brother by his activities... just to satisfy Hiranyakasipu." (SB 3.17.20)

questions.question: What did Hiranyaksa rest upon one of his shoulders?
questions.explanation: "He had anklets of gold tinkling about his feet, he was adorned with a gigantic garland, and he rested his huge mace on one of his shoulders." (SB 3.17.21)

questions.question: To what did the gods' hiding from Hiranyaksa compare?

options.text: Snakes hiding for fear of Garuda

questions.explanation: "The gods, therefore, were seized with fear at his very sight, and they hid themselves even as snakes hide themselves for fear of Garuda." (SB 3.17.22)

questions.question: What did Hiranyaksa do for the sake of sport after the demigods vanished?
questions.explanation: "...the mighty demon, who was like an elephant in wrath, for the sake of sport dived into the deep ocean, which was roaring terribly." (SB 3.17.24)

questions.question: With what weapon did Hiranyaksa smite the ocean waves as he traveled?
questions.explanation: "...the mighty Hiranyaksa smote the gigantic wind-tossed waves again and again with his iron mace and reached Vibhavari, the capital of Varuna." (SB 3.17.26)

questions.question: Vibhavari is the home of which lord of the aquatic creatures?
questions.explanation: "Vibhavari is the home of Varuna, lord of the aquatic creatures and guardian of the lower regions of the universe..." (SB 3.17.27)

questions.question: What did Hiranyaksa demand of Varuna upon reaching Vibhavari?
questions.explanation: "There Hiranyaksa fell at Varuna's feet like a lowborn man, and to make fun of him he said with a smile, 'Give me battle, O Supreme Lord!'" (SB 3.17.27)

questions.question: What reason did Varuna give for not fighting Hiranyaksa?

options.text: He had grown too old for combat
He was bound by a vow

questions.explanation: "O dear one, we have now desisted from warfare, having grown too old for combat." (SB 3.17.29)

questions.question: Whom did Varuna direct Hiranyaksa to fight for full satisfaction in battle?
questions.explanation: "You are so skilled in war that I do not see anyone else but the most ancient person, Lord Vishnu, who can give satisfaction in battle to you." (SB 3.17.30)

questions.question: Varuna predicted that on meeting that person, Hiranyaksa would lie down on the battlefield surrounded by what, for eternal sleep?
questions.explanation: "On reaching Him you will be rid of your pride at once and will lie down on the field of battle, surrounded by dogs, for eternal sleep." (SB 3.17.31)

questions.question: Which incarnation did Varuna name as one the Lord assumes to exterminate the wicked?
questions.explanation: "...He assumes His various incarnations like Varaha." (SB 3.17.31)

topics.name: Chapter 18: The Battle Between Lord Boar and the Demon Hiranyaksa

questions.question: From whom did Hiranyaksa learn the whereabouts of the Supreme Personality of Godhead?
questions.explanation: "...he learned from Narada the whereabouts of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and hurriedly betook himself to the depths of the ocean." (SB 3.18.1)

questions.question: In what form did Hiranyaksa find the Lord, bearing the earth on His tusks?
questions.explanation: "He saw there the all-powerful Personality of Godhead in His boar incarnation, bearing the earth upward on the ends of His tusks..." (SB 3.18.2)

questions.question: How did the demon mockingly address the Lord upon seeing Him?
questions.explanation: "The demon laughed: Oh, an amphibious beast!" (SB 3.18.2)

questions.question: With what did the demon threaten to smash the Lord's skull?

options.text: The mace hurled by his arms

questions.explanation: "When You fall dead with Your skull smashed by the mace hurled by my arms, the demigods and sages... will also automatically cease to exist, like trees without roots." (SB 3.18.5)

questions.question: To what did the Lord's rising from the water with the earth compare?

options.text: An elephant emerging with its female companion when assailed by an alligator

questions.explanation: "...He rose out of the water just as an elephant emerges with its female companion when assailed by an alligator." (SB 3.18.6)

questions.question: Where did the Lord place the earth, transferring to her the ability to float?

options.text: On the surface of the water

questions.explanation: "The Lord placed the earth within His sight on the surface of the water and transferred to her His own energy in the form of the ability to float on the water." (SB 3.18.8)

questions.question: Whom did the Lord describe as the hunting dogs He searches for?

options.text: Creatures like the demon, bound by the laws of death

questions.explanation: "The Personality of Godhead said: Indeed, We are creatures of the jungle, and We are searching after hunting dogs like you." (SB 3.18.10)

questions.question: When challenged by the Lord, the demon trembled in anger like what?
questions.explanation: "The demon, being thus challenged by the Personality of Godhead, became angry and agitated, and he trembled in anger like a challenged cobra." (SB 3.18.13)

questions.question: How did the Lord avoid the demon's first violent mace-blow aimed at His breast?

options.text: He moved slightly aside, as a yogi would elude death
He blocked it with His tusks

questions.explanation: "The Lord, however, by moving slightly aside, dodged the violent mace-blow aimed at His breast by the enemy, just as an accomplished yogi would elude death." (SB 3.18.15)

questions.question: With His mace, where did the Lord strike the demon?

options.text: On the right of his brow

questions.explanation: "Then with His mace the Lord struck the enemy on the right of his brow..." (SB 3.18.17)

questions.question: The name 'Haryaksa' in this chapter refers to which demon?
questions.explanation: "In this way, the demon Haryaksa and the Lord, the Personality of Godhead, struck each other with their huge maces..." (SB 3.18.18)

questions.question: The contest between the two combatants was compared to what?

options.text: Two forceful bulls fighting for the sake of a cow

questions.explanation: "...their contest looked like an encounter between two forceful bulls for the sake of a cow." (SB 3.18.19)

questions.question: Who came, with his followers, to see the terrible fight between the demon and the boar?

options.text: Brahma, the most independent demigod of the universe

questions.explanation: "...Brahma, the most independent demigod of the universe, accompanied by his followers, came to see the terrible fight..." (SB 3.18.20)

questions.question: For the first time, Narayana was assuming what form, which Brahma observed?
questions.explanation: "Brahma then addressed Narayana, who was assuming the form of a boar for the first time." (SB 3.18.21)

questions.question: What did Brahma say about the serpentine demon, advising the Lord not to play with him?

options.text: He is always very skilled in conjuring tricks and is arrogant

questions.explanation: "...there is no need to play with this serpentine demon, who is always very skilled in conjuring tricks and is arrogant, self-sufficient and most wicked." (SB 3.18.24)

questions.question: Before what hour did Brahma urge the Lord to kill the demon?
questions.explanation: "Please kill this sinful demon before the demoniac hour arrives and he presents another formidable approach favorable to him." (SB 3.18.25)

questions.question: Which auspicious period, most opportune for victory, did Brahma say had commenced at midday?
questions.explanation: "The auspicious period known as abhijit, which is most opportune for victory, commenced at midday and has all but passed..." (SB 3.18.27)

topics.name: Chapter 19: The Killing of the Demon Hiranyaksa

questions.question: How did the Lord react after hearing Brahma's prayer?

options.text: He heartily laughed and accepted it with a glance laden with love

questions.explanation: "...the Lord heartily laughed and accepted his prayer with a glance laden with love." (SB 3.19.1)

questions.question: From which part of Brahma had the Lord (as boar) appeared?
questions.explanation: "The Lord, who had appeared from the nostril of Brahma, sprang and aimed His mace at the chin of His enemy..." (SB 3.19.2)

questions.question: What happened to the Lord's mace when struck by the demon's mace?

options.text: It slipped from His hand and fell down whirling

questions.explanation: "Struck by the demon's mace, however, the Lord's mace slipped from His hand and looked splendid as it fell down whirling." (SB 3.19.3)

questions.question: Why did the demon not strike the Lord while He was unarmed?

options.text: He respected the law of single combat

questions.explanation: "...he respected the law of single combat, thereby kindling the fury of the Supreme Lord." (SB 3.19.4)

questions.question: Which weapon did the Lord invoke after His mace fell, acknowledging the demon's love of righteousness?
questions.explanation: "...the Personality of Godhead acknowledged the demon's love of righteousness and therefore invoked His Sudarsana discus." (SB 3.19.5)

questions.question: With what did the Lord, in His boar form, knock down the demon's mace as it came at Him?
questions.explanation: "...the Lord in His boar form, the enjoyer of all sacrificial offerings, playfully knocked down the mace with His left foot..." (SB 3.19.9)

questions.question: How did the Lord catch the mace the demon flung at Him?

options.text: With the same ease as Garuda would seize a serpent

questions.explanation: "...He stood firmly where He was and caught it with the same ease as Garuda, the king of birds, would seize a serpent." (SB 3.19.11)

questions.question: What weapon, 'as rapacious as a flaming fire,' did the demon next hurl at the Lord?
questions.explanation: "He now took a trident which was as rapacious as a flaming fire and hurled it against the Lord..." (SB 3.19.13)

questions.question: How did the Lord destroy the demon's flying trident?

options.text: He caught it with His foot
He tore it to pieces with His discus Sudarsana

questions.explanation: "The Personality of Godhead, however, tore it to pieces with His discus Sudarsana, which had a sharp-edged rim, even as Indra cut off a wing of Garuda." (SB 3.19.14)

questions.question: Where did the enraged demon strike the Lord with his fist, on a chest bearing what mark?
questions.explanation: "...struck his hard fist against the Lord's broad chest, which bore the mark of Srivatsa. Then he went out of sight." (SB 3.19.15)

questions.question: To what did the Lord's lack of any reaction to the demon's blow compare?

options.text: An elephant struck with a wreath of flowers

questions.explanation: "...the Lord... did not feel the least quaking in any part of His body, any more than an elephant would when struck with a wreath of flowers." (SB 3.19.16)

questions.question: During the demon's conjuring tricks, what did the sky rain down?

options.text: Pus, hair, blood, stool, urine and bones

questions.explanation: "The sky rained pus, hair, blood, stool, urine and bones." (SB 3.19.19)

questions.question: Whose heart shuddered as she recalled her husband Kasyapa's words during the battle?
questions.explanation: "At that very moment, a shudder suddenly ran through the heart of Diti, the mother of Hiranyaksa." (SB 3.19.23)

questions.question: Which weapon did the Lord discharge to disperse the demon's magical forces?
questions.explanation: "The Lord, the personal enjoyer of all sacrifices, now discharged His beloved Sudarsana, which was capable of dispersing the magical forces displayed by the demon." (SB 3.19.22)

questions.question: How did the Lord finally kill Hiranyaksa?

options.text: He cut his neck with the Sudarsana
He slapped him in the root of the ear, as Indra hit Vritra
He pierced him with an arrow
He crushed him with His mace

questions.explanation: "...Lord Adhoksaja slapped him in the root of the ear, even as Indra, the lord of the Maruts, hit the demon Vritra." (SB 3.19.25)

questions.question: To what did the demon's falling dead body compare?

options.text: A gigantic tree uprooted by the wind

questions.explanation: "...he fell down dead, like a gigantic tree uprooted by the wind." (SB 3.19.26)

questions.question: What did Brahma admiringly say upon seeing the dead demon's still-glowing face?

options.text: Oh, who could meet such blessed death?

questions.explanation: "...and Brahma admiringly said: Oh, who could meet such blessed death?" (SB 3.19.27)

questions.question: To whom did Maitreya narrate the Lord's first boar incarnation and the killing of Hiranyaksa?
questions.explanation: "Maitreya continued: My dear Vidura, I have explained to you the Personality of Godhead's coming down as the first boar incarnation and killing in a great fight a demon of unprecedented prowess..." (SB 3.19.32)

questions.question: By what name (meaning son of Kausara) is the sage Maitreya referred to in this chapter?
questions.explanation: "...by hearing the narration of the pastimes of the Supreme Personality of Godhead from the authoritative source of the sage Kausarava [Maitreya]..." (SB 3.19.33)

questions.question: What benediction is promised to one who hears the killing of Hiranyaksa?

options.text: Relief from sinful reactions, even the killing of a brahmana

questions.explanation: "...is at once relieved of the results of sinful activities, even the killing of a brahmana." (SB 3.19.37)

questions.question: Where is one transferred who listens to this narrative at the last moment of his life?

options.text: The supreme abode of the Lord

questions.explanation: "One who listens to it at the last moment of his life is transferred to the supreme abode of the Lord, O dear Saunaka." (SB 3.19.38)

topics.name: Chapter 20: Conversation Between Maitreya and Vidura

questions.question: Saunaka inquires what Svayambhuva Manu did after the earth was again situated in its orbit?

options.text: To show the path of liberation to persons to be born later

questions.explanation: "...what did Svayambhuva Manu do to show the path of liberation to persons who were to take birth later on?" (SB 3.20.1)

questions.question: From whose body was Vidura born?
questions.explanation: "Vidura was born from the body of Vedavyasa and was not less than he." (SB 3.20.3)

questions.question: At which holy place did Vidura meet the great sage who knew the science of spiritual life?
questions.explanation: "...at last he reached Hardwar, where he met the great sage who knew the science of spiritual life, and he inquired from him." (SB 3.20.4)

questions.question: Who was the son of Romaharsana that spoke at Naimisaranya?
questions.explanation: "On being asked to speak by the great sages of Naimisaranya, the son of Romaharsana, Suta Gosvami... said: Please hear what I shall now speak." (SB 3.20.7)

questions.question: By whose unseen activity, along with Maha-Vishnu and the force of time, was the equilibrium of the three modes agitated to produce the material elements?
questions.explanation: "When the equilibrium of the combination of the three modes of nature was agitated by the unseen activity of the living entity, by Maha-Vishnu and by the force of time, the total material elements were produced." (SB 3.20.12)

questions.question: For how long did the shiny egg lay on the Causal Ocean before the Lord entered it?
questions.explanation: "For over one thousand years the shiny egg lay on the waters of the Causal Ocean in the lifeless state. Then the Lord entered it as Garbhodakasayi Vishnu." (SB 3.20.15)

questions.question: From what did the lotus flower, reservoir of all conditioned souls, sprout?
questions.explanation: "From the navel of the Personality of Godhead Garbhodakasayi Vishnu sprouted a lotus flower effulgent like a thousand blazing suns." (SB 3.20.16)

questions.question: From what did Brahma first create the five coverings of ignorance of the conditioned souls?
questions.explanation: "First of all, Brahma created from his shadow the coverings of ignorance of the conditioned souls. They are five in number..." (SB 3.20.18)

questions.question: Which beings sprang for possession of the body of ignorance that Brahma threw off?
questions.explanation: "...Yakshas and Rakshasas sprang for possession of the body, which continued to exist in the form of night." (SB 3.20.19)

questions.question: What did Brahma drop before the chief demigods, which they sportingly took possession of?
questions.explanation: "He dropped before them the effulgent form of daytime, and the demigods sportingly took possession of it." (SB 3.20.22)

questions.question: From which part of his body did Brahma give birth to the demons, who were very fond of sex?
questions.explanation: "Lord Brahma then gave birth to the demons from his buttocks, and they were very fond of sex." (SB 3.20.23)

questions.question: Into what form did the impure body cast off by Brahma transform, which the asuras took for a damsel?
questions.explanation: "The body given up by Brahma took the form of the evening twilight, when the day and night meet, a time which kindles passion." (SB 3.20.29)

questions.question: From what did Brahma evolve the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsaras?
questions.explanation: "With a laugh full of deep significance, the worshipful Brahma then evolved by his own loveliness... the hosts of Gandharvas and Apsaras." (SB 3.20.38)

questions.question: Who gladly took possession of the shining form of moonlight that Brahma gave up?
questions.explanation: "After that, Brahma gave up that shining and beloved form of moonlight. Visvavasu and other Gandharvas gladly took possession of it." (SB 3.20.39)

questions.question: From his sloth, Brahma evolved which beings, closing his eyes when he saw them stand naked?
questions.explanation: "The glorious Brahma next evolved from his sloth the ghosts and fiends, but he closed his eyes when he saw them stand naked with their hair scattered." (SB 3.20.40)

questions.question: From his navel (his invisible form), Brahma evolved which hosts?
questions.explanation: "...evolved from his own invisible form, from his navel, the hosts of Sadhyas and Pitas." (SB 3.20.42)

questions.question: From his own reflection in the water, Brahma evolved which beings?
questions.explanation: "...admiring himself, he evolved Kimpurusas as well as Kinnaras out of that reflection." (SB 3.20.45)

questions.question: Into what did the hair that dropped from Brahma's full-length body transform?
questions.explanation: "...the hair that dropped from that body transformed into snakes, and even while the body crawled... there sprang from it ferocious serpents and Nagas with their hoods expanded." (SB 3.20.48)

questions.question: From what did Brahma evolve the Manus, who promote the welfare activities of the universe?
questions.explanation: "At that time he evolved from his mind the Manus, who promote the welfare activities of the universe." (SB 3.20.49)

questions.question: What form did the self-possessed creator give to the Manus?
questions.explanation: "The self-possessed creator gave them his own human form." (SB 3.20.50)

questions.question: Equipped with austere penance and devotion, Brahma finally evolved which beloved sons?
questions.explanation: "...Brahma, the self-born living creature, evolved great sages as his beloved sons." (SB 3.20.52)

topics.name: Chapter 21: Conversation Between Manu and Kardama

questions.question: Whose line or dynasty does Vidura ask Maitreya to describe at the opening of this chapter?
questions.explanation: "The line of Svāyambhuva Manu was most esteemed." (SB 3.21.1)

questions.question: Which two great sons of Svayambhuva Manu ruled the world of seven islands according to religious principles?
questions.explanation: "The two great sons of Svāyambhuva Manu — Priyavrata and Uttānapāda — ruled the world, consisting of seven islands." (SB 3.21.2)

questions.question: Devahuti, the daughter of Svayambhuva Manu, became the wife of which sage?
questions.explanation: "You have spoken of his daughter, known by the name Devahūti, as the wife of the sage Kardama." (SB 3.21.3)

questions.question: On the bank of which river did Kardama Muni practice penance after being commanded by Lord Brahma to beget children?
questions.explanation: "Kardama Muni practiced penance on the bank of the river Sarasvatī for a period of ten thousand years." (SB 3.21.6)

questions.question: For how long did Kardama Muni practice penance to propitiate the Personality of Godhead?
questions.explanation: "Kardama Muni practiced penance on the bank of the river Sarasvatī for a period of ten thousand years." (SB 3.21.6)

questions.question: In which yuga did the Supreme Personality of Godhead show Himself to Kardama Muni?
questions.explanation: "In the Satya-yuga, the lotus-eyed Supreme Personality of Godhead, being pleased, showed Himself to that Kardama Muni." (SB 3.21.8)

questions.question: What did the Lord hold in His fourth hand when He appeared before Kardama, besides the conch, disc and mace?
questions.explanation: "He held His characteristic conch, disc and mace in three of His hands and a white lily in the fourth." (SB 3.21.10)

questions.question: On whose shoulders did the Lord stand in the air when He appeared to Kardama Muni?
questions.explanation: "He stood in the air with His lotus feet placed on the shoulders of Garuḍa." (SB 3.21.11)

questions.question: Which famous gem hung suspended from the Lord's neck as He appeared before Kardama?
questions.explanation: "The famous Kaustubha gem suspended from His neck." (SB 3.21.11)

questions.question: According to Kardama's prayer, what does he describe as the true vessel to take one across the ocean of mundane nescience?
questions.explanation: "Your lotus feet are the true vessel to take one across the ocean of mundane nescience." (SB 3.21.14)

questions.question: What did Kardama Muni admit to desiring when he sought the shelter of the Lord's lotus feet in his prayer?

options.text: To marry a girl of like disposition

questions.explanation: "Desiring to marry a girl of like disposition who may prove to be a veritable cow of plenty in my married life." (SB 3.21.15)

questions.question: How many spokes does the Lord's wheel (described by Kardama) have?
questions.explanation: "It has thirteen spokes, 360 joints, six rims and numberless leaves carved upon it." (SB 3.21.18)

questions.question: To what does the Lord compare His creating and winding up of the universes by His own energies?
questions.explanation: "Just as a spider creates a cobweb by its own energy and again winds it up." (SB 3.21.19)

questions.question: The Lord told Kardama that He had already arranged for that for which Kardama worshiped Him, because He had come to know what was where?
questions.explanation: "Having come to know what was in your mind, I have already arranged for that for which you have worshiped Me." (SB 3.21.23)

questions.question: In which place does the Emperor Svayambhuva Manu have his seat, according to the Lord?
questions.explanation: "Has his seat in Brahmāvarta and rules over the earth with its seven oceans." (SB 3.21.25)

questions.question: What was the name of Svayambhuva Manu's queen, who would come with him to see Kardama?
questions.explanation: "That celebrated emperor... will come here with his queen, Śatarūpā, wishing to see you." (SB 3.21.26)

questions.question: How many daughters did the Lord foretell that Devahuti would bring forth for Kardama?
questions.explanation: "She will bring forth nine daughters from the seed sown in her by you." (SB 3.21.29)

questions.question: What did the Lord promise to manifest through Devahuti, along with the nine daughters?
questions.explanation: "I shall manifest My own plenary portion through your wife, Devahūti, along with your nine daughters." (SB 3.21.32)

questions.question: What is the name of the lake encircled by the river Sarasvati from which the Lord departed?
questions.explanation: "Departed from that lake called Bindu-sarovara, which was encircled by the river Sarasvatī." (SB 3.21.33)

questions.question: What was vibrated by the flapping wings of Garuda as the Lord left for Vaikuntha?

options.text: The hymns forming the basis of the Sama Veda

questions.explanation: "The hymns forming the basis of the Sāma Veda were vibrated by the flapping wings of the Lord's carrier, Garuḍa." (SB 3.21.34)

topics.name: Chapter 22: The Marriage of Kardama Muni and Devahuti

questions.question: From which part of Lord Brahma were the brahmanas created, according to Manu?
questions.explanation: "Lord Brahmā, the personified Veda, from his face created you, the brāhmaṇas." (SB 3.22.2)

questions.question: From which part of the thousand-legged Supreme Being were the kshatriyas created, for the protection of the brahmanas?
questions.explanation: "The thousand-legged Supreme Being created us, the kṣatriyas, from His thousand arms." (SB 3.22.3)

questions.question: Manu says the brahmanas are said to be the Lord's heart and the kshatriyas are said to be His what?
questions.explanation: "Hence the brāhmaṇas are said to be His heart and the kṣatriyas His arms." (SB 3.22.3)

questions.question: Of which two sons of Manu is Devahuti the sister?
questions.explanation: "My daughter is the sister of Priyavrata and Uttānapāda." (SB 3.22.9)

questions.question: From which sage had Devahuti heard of Kardama's noble character, learning and virtues, fixing her mind upon him?
questions.explanation: "The moment she heard from the sage Nārada of your noble character, learning, beautiful appearance, youth and other virtues, she fixed her mind upon you." (SB 3.22.10)

questions.question: Kardama said that the Vedic marriage could take place because Manu's daughter had not yet done what?

options.text: Married or given her word to anyone

questions.explanation: "Your daughter has not yet married or given her word to anyone. Therefore our marriage according to the Vedic system can take place." (SB 3.22.15)

questions.question: Which great Gandharva fell from his airplane after seeing Devahuti playing with a ball on the palace roof?
questions.explanation: "I have heard that Viśvāvasu, the great Gandharva... fell from his airplane after seeing your daughter playing with a ball on the roof of the palace." (SB 3.22.17)

questions.question: What condition did Kardama place before agreeing to marry Devahuti?

options.text: That he would never have children
That after she bears semen from his body, he would accept the life of devotional service
That she must remain a celibate ascetic
That they would always live in a palace

questions.explanation: "On the condition that after she bears semen from my body, I shall accept the life of devotional service accepted by the most perfect human beings." (SB 3.22.19)

questions.question: Whom did Kardama name as the highest authority for him, the origin of all the Prajapatis?

options.text: The unlimited Supreme Personality of Godhead

questions.explanation: "The highest authority for me is the unlimited Supreme Personality of Godhead... He is the origin of all Prajāpatis." (SB 3.22.20)

questions.question: Upon whom was the sage Kardama thinking when he became silent, his lotus-navel-bearing worshipable Lord?
questions.explanation: "The sage Kardama said this much only and then became silent, thinking of his worshipable Lord Viṣṇu, who has a lotus on His navel." (SB 3.22.21)

questions.question: Whose decision did the Emperor learn before gladly giving his daughter to Kardama, besides Devahuti's own?
questions.explanation: "After having unmistakably known the decision of the Queen, as well as that of Devahūti, the Emperor most gladly gave his daughter to the sage." (SB 3.22.22)

questions.question: Who lovingly gave the bride and bridegroom valuable presents such as jewelry, clothes and household articles in dowry?
questions.explanation: "Empress Śatarūpā lovingly gave most valuable presents... in dowry to the bride and bridegroom." (SB 3.22.23)

questions.question: How did Svayambhuva Manu react after handing over his daughter to Kardama?

options.text: His mind was agitated by feelings of separation and he embraced her

questions.explanation: "His mind agitated by feelings of separation, embraced his affectionate daughter with both his arms." (SB 3.22.24)

questions.question: As tears poured from Manu's eyes upon separation, what did he cry out?
questions.explanation: "As he cried, 'My dear mother! My dear daughter!'" (SB 3.22.25)

questions.question: From which place did Manu's subjects come forth to greet their returning lord with songs and music?
questions.explanation: "His subjects came forth from Brahmāvarta to greet their returning lord with songs, prayers and musical instruments." (SB 3.22.28)

questions.question: Upon entering which city did Manu return to his palace, where he had previously lived?
questions.explanation: "Having entered the city of Barhiṣmatī, in which he had previously lived, Manu entered his palace." (SB 3.22.32)

questions.question: Although absorbed in material happiness, why was Svayambhuva Manu not dragged to the lowest grade of life?

options.text: Because he enjoyed his happiness in a Krsna conscious atmosphere
Because he lived in the forest

questions.explanation: "He always enjoyed his material happiness in a Kṛṣṇa conscious atmosphere." (SB 3.22.34)

questions.question: For how many cycles of the four ages did Svayambhuva Manu pass his time, always thinking of Vasudeva?
questions.explanation: "He passed his time, which lasted seventy-one cycles of the four ages... always thinking of Vāsudeva." (SB 3.22.36)

questions.question: Out of compassion for all living entities, what did Svayambhuva Manu teach in reply to questions asked by certain sages?

options.text: The diverse sacred duties of men and the different varnas and asramas

questions.explanation: "He... taught the diverse sacred duties of men in general and the different varṇas and āśramas." (SB 3.22.38)

questions.question: After describing Svayambhuva Manu, whose flourishing does Maitreya say he will next speak of?
questions.explanation: "Please hear as I speak of the flourishing of his daughter Devahūti." (SB 3.22.39)

topics.name: Chapter 23: Devahuti's Lamentation

questions.question: After her parents departed, Devahuti served her husband constantly with great love, like which goddess serving Lord Siva?
questions.explanation: "The chaste woman Devahūti... served him constantly with great love, as Bhavānī, the wife of Lord Śiva, serves her husband." (SB 3.23.1)

questions.question: What did Devahuti give up while sanely and diligently pleasing her powerful husband?

options.text: Lust, pride, envy, greed, sinful activities and vanity

questions.explanation: "Giving up all lust, pride, envy, greed, sinful activities and vanity." (SB 3.23.3)

questions.question: Why was Kardama Muni astonished with Devahuti, expressing his pleasure with her?

options.text: She had neglected her own body to use it on his behalf

questions.explanation: "I am astonished that you have neglected your own body to use it on my behalf." (SB 3.23.6)

questions.question: Kardama said all material achievements are subject to be annihilated simply by what movement of Lord Visnu?
questions.explanation: "All material achievements are subject to be annihilated simply by a movement of the eyebrows of Lord Viṣṇu." (SB 3.23.8)

questions.question: Under whose protection did Devahuti acknowledge Kardama had achieved perfection and mastery of mystic powers?
questions.explanation: "You are the master of all the infallible mystic powers because you are under the protection of yoga-māyā, the transcendental nature." (SB 3.23.10)

questions.question: What did Devahuti remind Kardama he had promised, requesting he fulfill it?

options.text: Their bodily union, since children are a great quality for a chaste woman

questions.explanation: "You once made a promise that our bodily union should now fulfill, since children are a great quality for a chaste woman who has a glorious husband." (SB 3.23.10)

questions.question: By what means did Kardama instantly produce an aerial mansion to please Devahuti?

options.text: By the gift of Lord Brahma

questions.explanation: "The sage Kardama exercised his yogic power and instantly produced an aerial mansion that could travel at his will." (SB 3.23.12)

questions.question: In how many stories were the beds, couches, fans and seats of the aerial palace arranged?
questions.explanation: "The palace looked charming, with beds, couches, fans and seats, all separately arranged in seven stories." (SB 3.23.16)

questions.question: Why did the real swans in the palace repeatedly rise above the artificial swans and pigeons?

options.text: The artificial birds were so lifelike that the real ones thought them live birds

questions.explanation: "Artificial swans and pigeons so lifelike that the real swans rose above them again and again, thinking them live birds like themselves." (SB 3.23.20)

questions.question: Before mounting the aerial mansion, in which lake did Kardama tell Devahuti to bathe?
questions.explanation: "First bathe in Lake Bindu-sarovara, created by Lord Viṣṇu Himself, which can grant all the desires of a human being." (SB 3.23.23)

questions.question: How many girls in the prime of youth did Devahuti see in a house inside the lake?
questions.explanation: "In a house inside the lake she saw one thousand girls, all in the prime of youth and fragrant like lotuses." (SB 3.23.26)

questions.question: What did the damsels say to Devahuti when they suddenly rose with folded hands?
questions.explanation: "'We are your maidservants. Tell us what we can do for you.'" (SB 3.23.27)

questions.question: What sweet inebriating drink did the maidservants offer Devahuti along with food of all good qualities?
questions.explanation: "Next they offered her food containing all good qualities, and a sweet inebriating drink called āsavam." (SB 3.23.29)

questions.question: When Devahuti, transformed, thought of her husband, where did she appear?

options.text: At once where Kardama was, along with all the maidservants

questions.explanation: "She, along with all the maidservants, at once appeared where he was." (SB 3.23.34)

questions.question: In the aerial mansion, Kardama with his consort is compared to the moon in the midst of what?
questions.explanation: "Kardama Muni with his consort shone as charmingly as the moon in the midst of the stars in the sky." (SB 3.23.38)

questions.question: To the pleasure valleys of which mountain, where Kuvera generally enjoys, did Kardama travel in the aerial mansion?
questions.explanation: "In that aerial mansion he traveled to the pleasure valleys of Mount Meru." (SB 3.23.39)

questions.question: Into how many personalities did Kardama divide himself to give pleasure to Devahuti?
questions.explanation: "He divided himself into nine personalities just to give pleasure to Devahūti." (SB 3.23.44)

questions.question: How many female children did Devahuti give birth to, immediately, on the same day?
questions.explanation: "Devahūti gave birth to nine female children, all charming in every limb and fragrant with the scent of the red lotus flower." (SB 3.23.48)

questions.question: Besides fulfilling all his promises, what did Devahuti ask Kardama to give her as she was his surrendered soul?

options.text: A new husband for her daughters

questions.explanation: "You should give me fearlessness too." (SB 3.23.51)

questions.question: Devahuti laments that anyone whose work, religion and renunciation do not lead to devotional service must be considered what?
questions.explanation: "Must be considered dead, although he is breathing." (SB 3.23.56)

topics.name: Chapter 24: The Renunciation of Kardama Muni

questions.question: Whose words did Kardama recall as he replied to Devahuti's words full of renunciation?
questions.explanation: "Recalling the words of Lord Viṣṇu, the merciful sage Kardama replied as follows." (SB 3.24.1)

questions.question: What did Kardama tell Devahuti the infallible Supreme Personality of Godhead would shortly do?

options.text: Enter her womb as her son

questions.explanation: "The infallible Supreme Personality of Godhead will shortly enter your womb as your son." (SB 3.24.2)

questions.question: According to Kardama, the Lord will vanquish the knot of Devahuti's heart by becoming her son and teaching knowledge of what?
questions.explanation: "He will vanquish the knot of your heart by becoming your son and teaching knowledge of Brahman." (SB 3.24.4)

questions.question: How did the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Madhusudana, appear in Devahuti, having entered the semen of Kardama?

options.text: Just as light comes from the sun
Just as fire comes from wood in a sacrifice
Just as a river flows to the sea

questions.explanation: "Appeared in Devahūti just as fire comes from wood in a sacrifice." (SB 3.24.6)

questions.question: Who came along with Marichi and other sages to Kardama's hermitage at the Lord's appearance?
questions.explanation: "The first-born living being, went along with Marīci and other sages to the place of Kardama's hermitage." (SB 3.24.9)

questions.question: Brahma understood the Lord had appeared in Devahuti's womb to explain which system of knowledge?
questions.explanation: "Had appeared in the womb of Devahūti just to explain the complete state of knowledge known as sāṅkhya-yoga." (SB 3.24.10)

questions.question: Brahma said sons ought to obey the command of a father or spiritual master with due deference, saying what?
questions.explanation: "One should obey the command of his father or spiritual master with due deference, saying, 'Yes, sir.'" (SB 3.24.13)

questions.question: Brahma instructed Kardama to give away his nine daughters to whom?
questions.explanation: "Today please give away your daughters to the foremost of the sages." (SB 3.24.15)

questions.question: Brahma told Kardama the Supreme Personality of Godhead had assumed the body of which Muni?
questions.explanation: "He has now assumed the body of Kapila Muni." (SB 3.24.16)

questions.question: By what physical feature is Kapila Muni characterized, as described by Brahma?
questions.explanation: "Kapila Muni, who is characterized by His golden hair, His eyes just like lotus petals." (SB 3.24.17)

questions.question: Which demon does Brahma say the Supreme Lord, now within Devahuti's womb, had killed?
questions.explanation: "The same Supreme Personality of Godhead who killed the demon Kaiṭabha is now within your womb." (SB 3.24.18)

questions.question: By what name will Devahuti's son be celebrated among the people, as the head of all perfected souls?
questions.explanation: "Among the people He will be celebrated by the name Kapila." (SB 3.24.19)

questions.question: On what carrier did Lord Brahma, also known as Hamsa, return to the highest planetary system?
questions.explanation: "Lord Brahmā... went back to the highest of the three planetary systems on his swan carrier with the four Kumāras and Nārada." (SB 3.24.20)

questions.question: After Brahma's departure, to whom did Kardama hand over his nine daughters?

options.text: The nine great sages who created the population of the world

questions.explanation: "Kardama Muni... handed over his nine daughters, as instructed, to the nine great sages who created the population of the world." (SB 3.24.21)

questions.question: To which sage did Kardama deliver his daughter Santi, because of whom sacrificial ceremonies are well performed?
questions.explanation: "He delivered Śānti to Atharvā. Because of Śānti, sacrificial ceremonies are well performed." (SB 3.24.24)

questions.question: What order of life did Kardama wish to accept, having been liberated by the Lord from his debts to his father?

options.text: The order of an itinerant mendicant

questions.explanation: "I wish to accept the order of an itinerant mendicant." (SB 3.24.34)

questions.question: The Personality of Godhead Kapila said His appearance was especially to explain which philosophy?
questions.explanation: "My appearance in this world is especially to explain the philosophy of Sāṅkhya." (SB 3.24.36)

questions.question: Kapila said this path of self-realization had now been lost in the course of what?
questions.explanation: "This path of self-realization, which is difficult to understand, has now been lost in the course of time." (SB 3.24.37)

questions.question: To whom did Kapila say He would also describe this sublime knowledge so she could attain perfection?
questions.explanation: "I shall also describe this sublime knowledge, which is the door to spiritual life, to My mother." (SB 3.24.40)

questions.question: After being spoken to by his son Kapila, what vow did Kardama accept as he left for the forest?
questions.explanation: "The sage Kardama accepted silence as a vow in order to think of the Supreme Personality of Godhead." (SB 3.24.42)

questions.question: Freed from all hatred and desire, what did Kardama Muni ultimately attain?
questions.explanation: "Kardama Muni... ultimately attained the path back to Godhead." (SB 3.24.47)

topics.name: Chapter 25: The Glories of Devotional Service

questions.question: Although He is unborn, by what means did the Supreme Personality of Godhead take birth as Kapila Muni?

options.text: By the power of the sages

questions.explanation: "Although He is unborn, the Supreme Personality of Godhead took birth as Kapila Muni by His internal potency." (SB 3.25.1)

questions.question: For what purpose did Kapila descend?

options.text: To disseminate transcendental knowledge for the benefit of the whole human race

questions.explanation: "He descended to disseminate transcendental knowledge for the benefit of the whole human race." (SB 3.25.1)

questions.question: After Kardama left for the forest, why did Lord Kapila stay at the Bindu-sarovara?
questions.explanation: "Lord Kapila stayed on the strand of the Bindu-sarovara to please His mother, Devahuti." (SB 3.25.5)

questions.question: Why did Devahuti say she had fallen into the abyss of ignorance?

options.text: Because of the disturbance caused by her material senses
Because she had no spiritual master

questions.explanation: "I am very sick of the disturbance caused by my material senses, for because of this sense disturbance, my Lord, I have fallen into the abyss of ignorance." (SB 3.25.7)

questions.question: Devahuti describes the Lord as which instrument that can cut the tree of material existence?
questions.explanation: "You are the ax which can cut the tree of material existence." (SB 3.25.11)

questions.question: Why did Lord Kapila explain the path of the transcendentalists to His mother?

options.text: He was very keen to deliver her
It was a duty toward His mother
She had uncontaminated desire for transcendental realization

questions.explanation: "After hearing of His mother's uncontaminated desire for transcendental realization, the Lord thanked her within Himself for her questions." (SB 3.25.12)

questions.question: According to Kapila, when consciousness is attracted by the three modes of material nature, it is called what?
questions.explanation: "The stage in which the consciousness of the living entity is attracted by the three modes of material nature is called conditional life." (SB 3.25.15)

questions.question: Perfection in self-realization cannot be attained by any yogi unless he engages in what?

options.text: Devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead

questions.explanation: "Perfection in self-realization cannot be attained by any kind of yogi unless he engages in devotional service to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, for that is the only auspicious path." (SB 3.25.19)

questions.question: Material attachment, when applied to the self-realized devotees, does what?
questions.explanation: "But that same attachment, when applied to the self-realized devotees, opens the door of liberation." (SB 3.25.20)

questions.question: What are the symptoms of a sadhu, according to Lord Kapila?

options.text: Tolerant, merciful and friendly to all living entities

questions.explanation: "The symptoms of a sadhu are that he is tolerant, merciful and friendly to all living entities." (SB 3.25.21)

questions.question: Why do the sadhus not suffer from material miseries?

options.text: Because they are always filled with thoughts of the Lord's pastimes and activities
Because they live in the forest

questions.explanation: "The sadhus do not suffer from material miseries because they are always filled with thoughts of My pastimes and activities." (SB 3.25.23)

questions.question: According to Kapila, what is the easiest process of mystic power?
questions.explanation: "This process of Krsna consciousness is the easiest process of mystic power; when one is actually situated on that path of devotional service, he is able to control the mind." (SB 3.25.26)

questions.question: Kapila describes the Sankhya system of philosophy as what?

options.text: A combination of devotional service and mystic realization

questions.explanation: "He described the Sankhya system of philosophy, which is a combination of devotional service and mystic realization, as received by disciplic succession." (SB 3.25.31)

questions.question: What does bhakti, devotional service, do to the subtle body of the living entity?

options.text: Dissolves it without separate effort, just as fire in the stomach digests all that we eat
Transforms it into a spiritual body

questions.explanation: "Bhakti, devotional service, dissolves the subtle body of the living entity without separate effort, just as fire in the stomach digests all that we eat." (SB 3.25.33)

questions.question: Does a pure devotee attached to the Lord's service ever desire to become one with the Lord?

options.text: Only at the time of death
Never desires to become one with Me
Only if the Lord orders it

questions.explanation: "A pure devotee... never desires to become one with Me." (SB 3.25.34)

questions.question: When devotees accept the Lord as their friend, relative, son, preceptor, benefactor and Supreme Deity, what is the result?

options.text: They cannot be deprived of their possessions at any time

questions.explanation: "Because the devotees accept Me as their friend, their relative, their son, preceptor, benefactor and Supreme Deity, they cannot be deprived of their possessions at any time." (SB 3.25.38)

questions.question: Out of fear of whom do the wind, sun, Indra, fire and death perform their functions?
questions.explanation: "It is because of My supremacy that the wind blows, out of fear of Me; the sun shines out of fear of Me." (SB 3.25.42)

questions.question: According to Lord Kapila, what is the only means for attainment of the final perfection of life?

options.text: The intensive practice of devotional service

questions.explanation: "Therefore persons whose minds are fixed on the Lord engage in the intensive practice of devotional service. That is the only means for attainment of the final perfection of life." (SB 3.25.44)

topics.name: Chapter 26: Fundamental Principles of Material Nature

questions.question: Kapila says that knowing the different categories of the Absolute Truth releases a person from what?

options.text: The influence of the modes of material nature

questions.explanation: "I shall describe unto you the different categories of the Absolute Truth, knowing which any person can be released from the influence of the modes of material nature." (SB 3.26.1)

questions.question: According to Kapila, what is the ultimate perfection of self-realization?
questions.explanation: "Knowledge is the ultimate perfection of self-realization." (SB 3.26.2)

questions.question: Why is the Supreme Personality of Godhead perceivable everywhere?

options.text: Because of the modes of nature

questions.explanation: "He is perceivable everywhere because He is self-effulgent, and by His self-effulgent luster the entire creation is maintained." (SB 3.26.3)

questions.question: As His pastime, what did the Supreme Personality of Godhead accept?

options.text: The subtle material energy, invested with three material modes of nature

questions.explanation: "That Supreme Personality of Godhead, the greatest of the great, accepted the subtle material energy, which is invested with three material modes of nature and which is related with Visnu." (SB 3.26.4)

questions.question: What is the cause of one's conditional life?
questions.explanation: "Material consciousness is the cause of one's conditional life, in which conditions are enforced upon the living entity by the material energy." (SB 3.26.7)

questions.question: Devahuti asks Kapila to explain the characteristics of the Supreme Person and His energies, because both are the causes of what?
questions.explanation: "Kindly explain the characteristics of the Supreme Person and His energies, for both of these are the causes of this manifest and unmanifest creation." (SB 3.26.9)

questions.question: The unmanifested eternal combination of the three modes, the cause of the manifest state, is called what?
questions.explanation: "The unmanifested eternal combination of the three modes is the cause of the manifest state and is called pradhana." (SB 3.26.10)

questions.question: How many elements are included in the pradhana as described by Kapila?

options.text: The five gross, five subtle, four internal senses, five knowledge-gathering senses and five organs of action

questions.explanation: "The aggregate elements, namely the five gross elements, the five subtle elements, the four internal senses, the five senses for gathering knowledge and the five outward organs of action, are known as the pradhana." (SB 3.26.11)

questions.question: The mixing element, known as time, is counted as which element?
questions.explanation: "The mixing element, which is known as time, is counted as the twenty-fifth element." (SB 3.26.15)

questions.question: When the neutral, unmanifested nature is agitated, who is the time factor that causes creation to begin?
questions.explanation: "The time factor, as I have explained, is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, from whom the creation begins as a result of the agitation of the neutral, unmanifested nature." (SB 3.26.17)

questions.question: After the Lord impregnates material nature with His internal potency, material nature delivers the sum total of the cosmic intelligence, known as what?
questions.explanation: "Material nature delivers the sum total of the cosmic intelligence, which is known as Hiranmaya." (SB 3.26.19)

questions.question: The mode of goodness, the clear status of understanding the Personality of Godhead, is generally called what?
questions.explanation: "The mode of goodness, which is the clear, sober status of understanding the Personality of Godhead and which is generally called vasudeva, or consciousness, becomes manifest in the mahat-tattva." (SB 3.26.21)

questions.question: The threefold ahankara (false ego), the source of the gross elements, senses and mind, is known by what name?
questions.explanation: "It is known by the name of Sankarsana, who is directly Lord Ananta with a thousand heads." (SB 3.26.25)

questions.question: The mind of the living entity is known by the name of which Lord?
questions.explanation: "The mind of the living entity is known by the name of Lord Aniruddha, the supreme ruler of the senses." (SB 3.26.28)

questions.question: By transformation of the false ego in passion, what takes birth?
questions.explanation: "By transformation of the false ego in passion, intelligence takes birth, O virtuous lady." (SB 3.26.29)

questions.question: When egoism in ignorance is agitated by the sex energy of the Lord, which subtle element is manifested first?
questions.explanation: "When egoism in ignorance is agitated by the sex energy of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the subtle element sound is manifested, and from sound come the ethereal sky and the sense of hearing." (SB 3.26.32)

questions.question: From the interaction of fire and visual sensation, which subtle element evolves, from which water is produced?
questions.explanation: "By the interaction of fire and the visual sensation, the subtle element taste evolves under a superior arrangement. From taste, water is produced." (SB 3.26.41)

questions.question: Why do the peculiarities of all the elements exist in the earth alone?

options.text: Because earth is the largest element
Because the cause exists in its effect as well

questions.explanation: "Since the cause exists in its effect as well, the characteristics of the former are observed in the latter." (SB 3.26.49)

questions.question: In the universal egg, how does each layer compare to the previous one in thickness?

options.text: It is ten times bigger than the previous one

questions.explanation: "Each layer is ten times bigger than the previous one, and the final outside layer is covered by pradhana." (SB 3.26.52)

questions.question: When did the Cosmic Being (virat-purusa) finally arise from the causal waters?

options.text: When the god of fire entered His mouth
When Brahma entered His heart with intelligence
When the deity presiding over consciousness entered the heart with reason
When the sun-god entered His eyes

questions.explanation: "When the inner controller, the deity presiding over consciousness, entered the heart with reason, at that very moment the Cosmic Being arose from the causal waters." (SB 3.26.70)

topics.name: Chapter 27: Understanding Material Nature

questions.question: Although abiding in a material body, the living entity remains apart from the reactions of the modes, similar to what?

options.text: The sun remaining aloof from its reflection on water

questions.explanation: "He remains apart from the reactions of the modes, although abiding in a material body, just as the sun remains aloof from its reflection on water." (SB 3.27.1)

questions.question: When the soul identifies his body as the self under the spell of false ego, what does he think?

options.text: That he is the proprietor of everything
That he is a servant of God

questions.explanation: "By the influence of false ego he thinks that he is the proprietor of everything." (SB 3.27.2)

questions.question: Why does the conditioned soul transmigrate into different species of life, higher and lower?
